lessons.title: Built-in Microsoft Entra roles
lessons.short: Microsoft Entra built-in roles are Microsoft-managed bundles of directory permissions such as User Administrator, Helpdesk Administrator and Global Reader. Assign the least-privileged role that covers the task, and use role-assignable groups to assign roles to many admins at once.
lessons.deep:
A **role assignment** has three parts: a **role definition** (the permissions), a **security principal** (user, role-assignable group or service principal) and a **scope** (tenant, administrative unit or a single resource).

Built-in roles can't be edited. Common ones:
- **Global Administrator**: everything; keep to a few accounts plus emergency access accounts.
- **Privileged Role Administrator**: manages role assignments and PIM.
- **User Administrator**: creates and manages users and groups, resets passwords for many users.
- **Helpdesk Administrator**: resets passwords and invalidates refresh tokens for non-admins and some limited admins.
- **Groups Administrator**, **License Administrator**, **Global Reader** (read-only everywhere).

**Role-assignable groups** let you assign a role to a group. The setting *Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group* (`isAssignableToRole`) can only be set when the group is created, membership must be **Assigned** (no dynamic rules), a group can't be nested inside one, and a tenant can have up to **500**. They need Microsoft Entra ID P1. Creating one requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.

terms.d: The collection of permissions a role grants.
Where a role applies: tenant, administrative unit or a single resource.
A group created with isAssignableToRole = true so it can hold Entra role assignments.
Grant only the permissions needed for the task.

lessons.trap: Exams pick Global Administrator or User Administrator when a narrower role (Helpdesk, Groups, License Administrator) is enough, and assume an existing group can be made role-assignable later.
lessons.example: Contoso creates a role-assignable group 'Tier1-Helpdesk' and assigns it Helpdesk Administrator, so new support staff get rights just by joining the group.

lessons.title: Custom Microsoft Entra roles
lessons.short: When no built-in role fits, build a custom role from a preset list of permissions (for example microsoft.directory/applications/credentials/update). Each user assigned a custom role needs Microsoft Entra ID P1, and you need at least Privileged Role Administrator to create them.
lessons.deep:
A **custom role** is a role definition your organisation creates by picking permissions from a preset list. These are the same permission strings built-in roles use, and only permissions enabled for custom roles are offered. They cover app registrations, enterprise applications, consent, devices, users and groups. Permission strings follow the pattern `microsoft.directory/<resource>/<property>/<action>`, for example `microsoft.directory/applications/credentials/update` to rotate app secrets.

You create custom roles in **Roles & admins > New custom role**, or with Microsoft Graph PowerShell (`New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleDefinition`, then assign with `New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment`).

Key facts:
- Licensing: built-in roles are free, but custom role assignees need **Microsoft Entra ID P1**.
- Creating custom roles needs at least **Privileged Role Administrator**.
- Assignments can target the tenant, an administrative unit or a specific resource such as one app registration.
- Built-in roles can't be copied and edited in place; you build a new definition.
- Custom Entra roles are separate from **Azure RBAC** custom roles, which control Azure resources such as subscriptions.

terms.d: An organisation-defined Entra role built from preset permissions.
The list of permission strings inside a role definition's rolePermissions.
Separate role system for Azure resources (subscriptions, VMs), not directory objects.

lessons.trap: Don't confuse Entra custom roles with Azure RBAC custom roles, and remember custom roles cost P1 per assignee while built-in roles are free.
lessons.example: A team that only rotates app secrets gets a custom 'App Secret Rotator' role with the applications/credentials/update permission instead of Application Administrator.

lessons.title: When to use administrative units
lessons.short: Administrative units (AUs) are containers that limit an admin's role to a subset of users, groups or devices, such as one region, faculty or subsidiary. Recommend them when you need delegated, scoped administration inside a single tenant.
lessons.deep:
Without AUs, a Helpdesk Administrator can reset passwords for every non-admin user in the tenant. An **administrative unit** restricts a role assignment to the members of that unit, so a regional helpdesk only manages its own region.

Recommend AUs when:
- A university wants each school's IT staff to manage only that school's students.
- A multinational wants country teams to manage local users and devices.
- A subsidiary's admins should manage their own staff without tenant-wide rights.

They are **not** the answer when:
- You need to hide objects: AUs scope **management** only, and users can still browse the directory with default permissions.
- You need full isolation (separate policies, separate admins for everything): that is a separate tenant.
- You need just-in-time elevation: that is PIM, which can be combined with AU-scoped roles.
- You want to protect sensitive accounts even from tenant-wide admins: that is a **restricted management** AU.

Roles that can be scoped to an AU include User Administrator, Helpdesk Administrator, Groups Administrator, Authentication Administrator, License Administrator and Password Administrator. Global Administrator can't be AU-scoped.

terms.d: A container of users, groups or devices used to scope role assignments.
Giving local admins rights over only part of the directory.
A role assignment whose scope is an AU instead of the tenant.

lessons.trap: AUs don't hide users or create separate policies; the wrong answers are 'create another tenant' or 'use group owners' when scoped admin rights are all that's needed.
lessons.example: Fabrikam University creates AUs for Arts and Engineering and assigns each faculty's IT staff Helpdesk Administrator scoped to their AU.

lessons.title: Configure and manage administrative units
lessons.short: Create AUs in Roles & admins > Admin units, add users, groups or devices manually or by dynamic rules (users and devices only), then assign scoped roles. Creating AUs is free; each AU-scoped admin needs Microsoft Entra ID P1.
lessons.deep:
**Creating** an AU works in the Microsoft Entra admin center, Microsoft Graph or PowerShell. Then:
1. Add members: users, groups and devices can be added manually or by CSV.
2. Optionally set **dynamic membership** so users or devices join automatically by rule (for example `user.department -eq "Sales"`). Groups can't be added by dynamic rule, and an AU's membership is either assigned or dynamic.
3. Assign roles scoped to the AU under the AU's **Roles and administrators** page. With Graph the scope is `/administrativeUnits/<AU-id>`.

Rules and limits:
- AUs **can't be nested**.
- Adding a group to an AU lets scoped admins manage the **group** (name, membership), not automatically the users inside it. Add the users too if they should be managed.
- A role assigned to an AU applies to its members, not to the AU object itself.
- Licensing: AU members need Free; each **admin with an AU-scoped role needs P1**; dynamic AU membership needs P1 for members.
- Privileged Role Administrator (or Global Administrator) assigns AU-scoped roles.
- Intune device management isn't scoped by Entra AUs.

terms.d: Rule-based automatic membership for users or devices in an AU.
The scope value in a Graph role assignment, e.g. /administrativeUnits/{id}.
A role assignment that applies only to members of an AU.

lessons.trap: Exams claim AUs can be nested or that groups can be added dynamically; both are false.
lessons.example: An AU 'Germany' uses the rule user.country -eq "DE" so new German hires automatically fall under the German helpdesk.

lessons.title: Restricted management administrative units
lessons.short: A restricted management AU protects its members (users, devices, security groups) from changes by anyone without a role assigned at that AU's scope, even tenant-wide admins and Global Administrators. The setting is chosen at creation and can't be changed later.
lessons.deep:
Normal AUs **add** scoped admins. **Restricted management administrative units** also **block** tenant-level admins from modifying members, which is ideal for executive accounts or sensitive security groups.

How it works:
- Only admins explicitly assigned a role scoped to the restricted AU can modify its objects' Entra properties.
- Tenant-scoped User, Helpdesk and Groups Administrators are blocked, and so are group/device owners.
- **Global Administrators and Privileged Role Administrators** can't modify the objects either, but they can manage the AU itself (create/delete it, add/remove members, assign scoped roles), so a Global Administrator could assign themselves a scoped role, which is audited.
- Supported members: **users, devices and security groups**. Microsoft 365 groups, mail-enabled security groups and distribution groups aren't supported.
- **Restricted management** must be set when the AU is created; it can't be switched on or off later.
- Members can't be managed by Entra ID Governance features such as PIM, entitlement management, lifecycle workflows or access reviews.
- Licensing matches normal AUs: P1 for scoped admins. Maximum 100 restricted AUs per tenant.

terms.d: An AU whose members can only be changed by admins scoped to it.
An admin whose role applies across the whole tenant.

lessons.trap: A normal AU never removes tenant-wide admins' rights; only a restricted management AU does, and it must be chosen at creation.
lessons.example: Contoso places its CEO and CFO accounts in a restricted management AU so only the executive-support team, assigned User Administrator on that AU, can change them.

lessons.title: Evaluate effective permissions for Entra roles
lessons.short: A user's effective permissions are the combination of every active role assignment they hold, directly or through role-assignable groups, each limited by its scope. Check a user's Assigned roles page to see roles, scopes and whether each came directly or from a group.
lessons.deep:
To work out what someone can actually do:
1. **List all assignments**: Users > select user > **Assigned roles**. It shows each role, its scope and whether it was assigned directly or inherited through a group. With P2/PIM it also shows **eligible**, **active** and expired assignments.
2. **Apply scope**: a tenant-scoped role applies everywhere; an AU-scoped role only to AU members; a resource-scoped role (for example one app registration) only to that resource. A role scoped to a container applies to the objects inside it, not the container object itself.
3. **Combine**: permissions from all active roles add together. There are no deny assignments in Entra roles (restricted management AUs are the exception that blocks tenant admins).
4. **Eligible isn't effective**: a PIM-eligible role grants nothing until activated.
5. Remember **default user permissions** and object ownership (for example, owners of a group can manage its membership).

Tools: **Roles & admins > All roles > Download assignments** exports a CSV of active assignments. In PowerShell, `Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment -Filter "principalId eq '<id>'"` lists direct assignments.

terms.d: Everything a principal can do once all active assignments and scopes are combined.
PIM assignment that must be activated before it grants permissions.
Per-user/per-group page showing roles, scope and assignment path.

lessons.trap: Candidates forget that AU-scoped rights stop at AU members and that an eligible PIM role gives no rights until activation.
lessons.example: Ana has Helpdesk Administrator at tenant scope and User Administrator on the Sales AU: she can reset any non-admin's password, but can only create or delete users in Sales.

lessons.title: Custom domain names in Entra ID and Microsoft 365
lessons.short: Every tenant starts with a permanent initial domain (contoso.onmicrosoft.com). Add custom domains, prove ownership with a TXT or MX DNS record, then set one as primary for new users. A domain can be verified in only one tenant at a time.
lessons.deep:
**Initial domain**: `<name>.onmicrosoft.com`, created with the tenant; it **can't be changed or deleted**.

**Adding a custom domain** (at least **Domain Name Administrator**):
1. Entra ID > Domain names > **Add custom domain** and type the full name including the top-level suffix (for example `contoso.com`).
2. Copy the DNS values shown and create a **TXT** (or **MX**) record at the registrar; TTL is typically 3600 seconds.
3. Select **Verify**. Propagation can take minutes to days; if you made a mistake, wait for the TTL to expire.
4. Optionally **Make primary**, so new users default to `@contoso.com`, and update existing users' UPNs.

Rules worth knowing:
- A domain can be verified in **only one directory**. To move it, remove it from the old tenant first, which means removing references to it (user UPNs, email addresses, groups, apps).
- The Microsoft 365 admin center offers the same flow and adds service records (MX, CNAME for Autodiscover, SPF) for Exchange and Teams.
- A domain can be **managed** (cloud auth) or **federated** (for example with AD FS); federation is changed with Entra Connect or `Update-MgDomain`.
- An unmanaged (self-service sign-up) tenant holding the domain can block verification until an admin takeover.

terms.d: The permanent onmicrosoft.com domain created with the tenant.
The default domain suffix for newly created users.
DNS record proving you own the domain.
A domain whose authentication is redirected to an external IdP like AD FS.

lessons.trap: CNAME is a common wrong answer for verification, and the initial onmicrosoft.com domain can't be removed.
lessons.example: After acquiring Tailspin, Contoso removes tailspin.com from Tailspin's old tenant, then adds and verifies it in Contoso's tenant with a TXT record.

lessons.title: Company branding
lessons.short: Company branding customises the Microsoft sign-in page with your logos, background, colours, sign-in text and SSPR link. Configure a default experience and optional browser-language versions; it needs Entra ID P1/P2 (or certain Microsoft 365 plans) and at least Organizational Branding Administrator.
lessons.deep:
Company branding lives in **Entra ID > Custom branding**. You edit the **default sign-in experience** and can **Add browser language** versions that override the default for users whose browser uses that language; unchanged elements fall back to the default.

What you can set:
- Favicon (32x32 px), background image (1920x1080 px, max 300 KB), banner logo (245x36 px), square logos for light and dark themes (240x240 px). PNG preferred.
- Page background colour, header and footer, privacy and terms links.
- **Sign-in page text** up to 1,024 Unicode characters; it's public, so no secrets.
- **Show self-service password reset (SSPR)** and username hint text.

When branding appears:
- On multitenant Microsoft sites (myapps, outlook.com), branding shows **after** the user types their username and selects Next, because only then is the tenant known.
- Add a home realm hint such as `?whr=contoso.com` to an app URL to show branding on the very first screen.
- **B2B guests** see their **home tenant's** branding.

Licensing: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, Microsoft 365 Business Standard or SharePoint (Plan 1). Minimum role: **Organizational Branding Administrator**. Custom CSS is being restricted for newer tenants, so rely on the standard settings.

terms.d: Branding applied to all sign-ins to the tenant.
Language-specific branding overriding the default.
Home realm hint in a URL that lets branding appear before username entry.

lessons.trap: Exams suggest branding is missing because of a licence issue, when it's simply that the tenant isn't known until the username is entered (fix with whr=).
lessons.example: Contoso shares https://myapps.microsoft.com/?whr=contoso.com so staff see the Contoso logo and helpdesk text immediately.

lessons.title: Tenant properties and user settings
lessons.short: Tenant properties hold the organisation name, country/region, technical contact, privacy contact and privacy statement URL, plus the Global Administrator toggle 'Access management for Azure resources'. User settings control what members can do by default, such as registering apps or creating tenants.
lessons.deep:
**Tenant properties** (Entra ID > Overview > Properties):
- Name, **country or region** (set at creation; determines data location and can't be changed later), tenant ID.
- **Technical contact**, **Global privacy contact** and **Privacy statement URL**. Privacy information is shown to guests and is needed before external users can be allowed to remove themselves.
- **Access management for Azure resources**: when a Global Administrator sets it to Yes, they get **User Access Administrator** at the Azure root scope (all subscriptions and management groups). Use it to regain access, then set it back to No.

**User settings** (Entra ID > Users > User settings):
- **Users can register applications** (default Yes).
- **Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants** (Yes limits this to the Tenant Creator role).
- **Users can create security groups** and Microsoft 365 group creation.
- **Restrict access to Microsoft Entra admin center**: hides common admin pages from non-admins, but isn't a security control: Graph and PowerShell still work. Use Conditional Access on the Windows Azure Service Management API to really block it.
- **LinkedIn account connections**.
- **Guest user access** and invite settings are in External collaboration settings.

terms.d: Toggle that grants a Global Administrator User Access Administrator at Azure root scope.
Person contacted about data privacy; required for some external user features.
Role allowed to create tenants when non-admin creation is restricted.

lessons.trap: 'Restrict access to Microsoft Entra admin center' is often chosen as a security control; it doesn't block Graph or PowerShell.
lessons.example: A Global Administrator who lost access to an orphaned Azure subscription flips Access management for Azure resources to Yes, fixes RBAC, then turns it off.

lessons.title: Group and device settings
lessons.short: Group settings control self-service group management, who can create security and Microsoft 365 groups, expiration and naming policies. Device settings control who may join or register devices, MFA for joining, device limits, extra local administrators, LAPS and BitLocker key self-recovery.
lessons.deep:
**Group settings** (Entra ID > Groups > General):
- **Owners can manage group membership requests in My Groups** and restrict access to groups features in My Groups.
- **Users can create security groups** / **Microsoft 365 groups** in portals, API or PowerShell.
- **Expiration**: a lifetime (for example 180 or 365 days, or custom) for **Microsoft 365 groups**; owners get renewal emails and active groups renew automatically. Deleted Microsoft 365 groups can be restored for 30 days.
- **Naming policy**: prefix/suffix and blocked words for Microsoft 365 groups. Expiration and naming policies need Entra ID P1.

**Device settings** (Entra ID > Devices > Device settings, Cloud Device Administrator can change):
- **Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra ID**: default All.
- **Users may register their devices**: needed for BYOD and Intune enrolment of personal devices.
- **Require MFA to register or join devices**: default No; Microsoft recommends the Conditional Access user action **Register or join devices** instead (leave this setting at No when you do).
- **Maximum number of devices per user**: default **50**, up to 100; doesn't apply to hybrid joined devices.
- **Additional local administrators** on Entra joined devices, and whether the registering user becomes local admin.
- **Enable Microsoft Entra LAPS** and **Restrict non-admin users from recovering BitLocker keys**.

terms.d: Lifetime after which unused Microsoft 365 groups are deleted unless renewed.
Conditional Access user action to require MFA when joining/registering devices.
Rotates and stores the local admin password of Entra joined devices.

lessons.trap: For MFA on device join, the recommended answer is the Conditional Access user action, not the legacy device setting.
lessons.example: Contoso sets a 365-day expiration on Microsoft 365 groups and limits device joins to the 'Corp-Device-Joiners' group.

lessons.title: Create, configure and manage users
lessons.short: Create cloud users or invite guests in Entra ID > Users, set UPN, usage location and profile properties, and reset passwords or revoke sessions. Deleted users stay soft-deleted for 30 days and can be restored; synced users are managed in on-premises AD.
lessons.deep:
**User types**: **Member** (internal staff) or **Guest** (external). The **source** is either cloud-only or synced from on-premises AD by Entra Connect / Cloud Sync.

**Creating a user** (at least **User Administrator**): set display name, **user principal name (UPN)** using a verified domain, an initial password, and properties like job title, department, manager and **usage location** (required before licences with location-restricted services can be assigned). In Graph PowerShell: `New-MgUser` with `-DisplayName`, `-UserPrincipalName`, `-MailNickname`, `-AccountEnabled` and `-PasswordProfile`.

**Managing users**: reset password, require re-registration of MFA, **Revoke sessions** (invalidates refresh tokens), block sign-in (`accountEnabled = false`), edit properties.

**Synced users**: attributes that come from AD (name, department, UPN) are changed in AD, not in the cloud; the next sync would overwrite them.

**Deleting and restoring**: deleted users are **soft-deleted for 30 days** (Users > Deleted users). Restoring brings back the account with its properties and licences, even if no licences are free. After 30 days, or after **Delete permanently**, the account can't be recovered, even by Microsoft support.

terms.d: User principal name, the sign-in name like user@contoso.com.
Country of use, required before many licences can be assigned.
30-day recoverable state after a user is deleted.
Invalidates refresh tokens so the user must sign in again.

lessons.trap: Exams offer 'edit the department in Entra ID' for a synced user; the change must be made in on-premises AD.
lessons.example: A user deleted by mistake 12 days ago is restored from Deleted users with her licences and properties intact.

lessons.title: Create, configure and manage groups
lessons.short: Entra ID has security groups (access to resources, can hold users, devices, service principals and other groups) and Microsoft 365 groups (collaboration: shared mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site; users only). Membership is Assigned, Dynamic user or Dynamic device.
lessons.deep:
**Group types**
- **Security group**: grants access to apps, resources and licences. Members can be users, devices, service principals and other groups.
- **Microsoft 365 group**: collaboration group that provisions a shared mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site and Planner; members are **users only** (members and guests).
- Mail-enabled security groups and distribution lists are managed mostly from Exchange.

**Membership types**
- **Assigned**: owners or admins add members.
- **Dynamic user** / **Dynamic device**: a rule adds and removes members automatically; you can't add or remove members manually. A group can't mix users and devices.

**Owners** can manage membership (and approve join requests if self-service is enabled in My Groups). **Groups Administrator** manages all groups; **User Administrator** can too.

**Lifecycle**: Microsoft 365 groups support **expiration** and **naming policies** (P1) and can be restored for 30 days after deletion.

Groups power **group-based licensing**, app assignment, Conditional Access targeting, access reviews and role assignment (role-assignable groups only).

terms.d: Group used for access control; can contain users, devices, groups and service principals.
Collaboration group with shared mailbox, calendar and SharePoint; users only.
Members are added manually.

lessons.trap: Microsoft 365 groups can't contain devices or other groups; a device-based dynamic group must be a security group.
lessons.example: Contoso uses a Microsoft 365 group for the Marketing team's shared mailbox and a security group to grant the team access to a SaaS app.

lessons.title: Dynamic membership rules
lessons.short: Dynamic membership groups use rules like user.department -eq "Sales" to add and remove members automatically. Each unique user in a dynamic group needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 coverage; device-only groups need no licence.
lessons.deep:
A rule has the form `<property> <operator> <value>`, for example `user.department -eq "Sales"` or `device.deviceOSType -eq "Windows"`.

**Operators**: `-eq`, `-ne`, `-startsWith`, `-notStartsWith`, `-endsWith`, `-contains`, `-notContains`, `-match`, `-notMatch` (regex), `-in`, `-notIn`. Combine expressions with `-and`, `-or`, `-not` and brackets: `(user.department -eq "Sales") -or (user.department -eq "Marketing")`.

**Special rules**
- All members only (exclude guests): `(user.objectId -ne null) -and (user.userType -eq "Member")`. Without the second clause, guests are included.
- **Direct reports**: `Direct Reports for "<manager objectId>"` (direct reports only, can't be combined with other rules).

**Rule builder vs text box**: the builder handles up to five expressions for user rules; device rules, `-contains` or complex rules need the text editor. Rule body max 3,072 characters; up to 15,000 dynamic groups per tenant.

**Licensing**: the tenant needs enough **P1** licences for every unique user who is a member of any dynamic group (no need to assign them to those users). Device-based groups need none.

Use **Validate rules** to test users against a rule before saving.

terms.d: Expression that determines group membership automatically.
Regular-expression operator; use sparingly for performance.
Special rule that adds a manager's direct reports.

lessons.trap: user.objectId -ne null includes guests; to get only employees add user.userType -eq "Member".
lessons.example: The rule user.jobTitle -startsWith "Engineer" keeps the Engineering group current as people change roles.

lessons.title: Custom security attributes
lessons.short: Custom security attributes are business-specific key-value attributes (grouped into attribute sets) that you add to users and service principals for sensitive data and attribute-based access control. Even Global Administrators can't read or assign them by default; dedicated Attribute roles are required.
lessons.deep:
**Structure**: an **attribute set** (for example `Engineering`) contains **attribute definitions** (for example `Project`, data type String). Data types are **String, Integer and Boolean**; strings and integers can be multi-valued, and you can require **predefined values only**.

**Roles** (assignable at tenant or attribute-set scope):
- **Attribute Definition Administrator**: create and manage sets and definitions.
- **Attribute Assignment Administrator**: assign values to users and service principals.
- **Attribute Definition Reader** / **Attribute Assignment Reader**: read only.
- **Attribute Log Reader / Administrator**: read audit logs for attribute changes, configure diagnostic settings.
By default, **Global Administrator and other admin roles can't read, define or assign** them, which keeps sensitive values (like a security clearance) separate from general admins.

**Rules**: names (32 chars, no spaces) **can't be renamed**; descriptions can change. Definitions can be deactivated, not deleted. 'Only allow predefined values' can change from Yes to No but not back. Limits: 500 active definitions and 500 sets per tenant, 50 values per object.

Uses: filtering apps, Azure ABAC role conditions on storage, and scoping. Available in all Entra ID editions.

terms.d: A container that groups related custom security attributes.
Role that assigns attribute values to users and apps.
Attribute-based access control using attributes in authorisation decisions.

lessons.trap: Global Administrator isn't enough to manage custom security attributes; assign the specific Attribute role.
lessons.example: HR uses an attribute set 'Compliance' with attribute 'Clearance' (predefined values Confidential, Secret) assigned by the security office only.

lessons.title: Bulk operations in the Entra admin center
lessons.short: The Entra admin center supports CSV-based bulk create, bulk invite, bulk delete, bulk restore and download of users, plus bulk member import/removal for groups. Download the template, fill it in, upload it, and check Bulk operation results.
lessons.deep:
**Bulk operations** live on the Users (and Groups) pages under **Bulk operations**:
- **Bulk create**: creates internal **member** accounts. Required template columns: **Name [displayName]**, **User name [userPrincipalName]** and **Initial password [passwordProfile]**. No invitation emails are sent; passwords must meet policy.
- **Bulk invite**: creates **guest** accounts and sends B2B invitations. Requires email address to invite and redirection URL.
- **Bulk delete** (by UPN) and **Bulk restore** (by object ID) for soft-deleted users.
- **Download users** to CSV, and for groups **Import members**, **Remove members** and **Download members**.

Process:
1. Download the latest CSV template (keep the version and header rows, delete the sample row).
2. Fill one row per object.
3. Upload; the file is validated before submission.
4. Check **Bulk operation results** for status and download error details.

Limits: a bulk job that doesn't finish within about **one hour** can fail, so split large files. Minimum role for bulk user create is **User Administrator**. For very large or repeatable jobs, use Microsoft Graph PowerShell instead.

terms.d: CSV upload that creates member user accounts.
CSV upload that creates guest accounts and sends invitations.
Page that tracks bulk job status and errors.

lessons.trap: Bulk create can't create guests or send invitations; that's Bulk invite.
lessons.example: Before term starts, a school bulk-creates 800 student accounts from a CSV exported from its student system.

lessons.title: Automating with Microsoft Graph PowerShell
lessons.short: Microsoft Graph PowerShell (Microsoft.Graph module) replaces the retired MSOnline and AzureAD modules. Connect with Connect-MgGraph and the scopes you need, then use cmdlets like Get-MgUser, New-MgUser, Update-MgUser, New-MgGroup and Set-MgUserLicense in scripts.
lessons.deep:
**Connecting**: `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "User.ReadWrite.All","Group.ReadWrite.All"` signs in with delegated permissions; consent to the requested scopes is required. Unattended scripts use an app registration with a certificate or a managed identity and **application permissions**.

**Common cmdlets** (verb-Mg-noun pattern):
- `Get-MgUser -All -Filter "department eq 'Sales'"` and `-Property` to request specific fields.
- `New-MgUser`, `Update-MgUser`, `Remove-MgUser`.
- `New-MgGroup`, `New-MgGroupMember`, `Get-MgGroupMember`.
- `Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $id -AddLicenses @(@{SkuId=$sku}) -RemoveLicenses @()` and `Get-MgSubscribedSku`.
- `Invoke-MgGraphRequest` for any Graph REST call.

**Bulk pattern**: `Import-Csv users.csv | ForEach-Object { New-MgUser ... }`.

Advanced queries (some filters, `$count`, `-Search`) need `-ConsistencyLevel eventual`.

Why it matters: the MSOnline and AzureAD PowerShell modules are **retired**, so exam answers should use Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets (Mg prefix) or the Microsoft Graph API.

terms.d: Signs in to Microsoft Graph PowerShell with chosen scopes.
A permission such as User.ReadWrite.All requested at sign-in.
App-only permission used by unattended scripts.

lessons.trap: Answers using MSOnline (Set-MsolUser) or AzureAD (New-AzureADUser) cmdlets are outdated; prefer Mg cmdlets.
lessons.example: A nightly script connects with a certificate-based app registration and sets usage location for all users missing it.

lessons.title: Device identity: registered, joined, hybrid joined
lessons.short: Microsoft Entra registered suits personal (BYOD) and mobile devices; Microsoft Entra joined suits organisation-owned Windows devices signing in with work accounts; Microsoft Entra hybrid joined is for devices joined to on-premises AD and also registered in Entra ID.
lessons.deep:
A device identity lets Conditional Access, Intune and SSO recognise the device.

- **Microsoft Entra registered**: personal Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android and macOS devices. The user signs in to the device with a personal account and adds a work account. Typical for BYOD with Intune app or MDM enrolment.
- **Microsoft Entra joined**: organisation-owned Windows 10/11 devices (and Windows Server 2019+ VMs in Azure). Users sign in with their Entra work account; no on-premises AD join needed. Provisioned by OOBE, Windows Autopilot or bulk enrolment. Gives SSO to cloud and, with line of sight, on-premises resources.
- **Microsoft Entra hybrid joined**: Windows devices joined to on-premises **AD DS** and registered in Entra ID. Needs Entra Connect (or Cloud Sync device sync) to sync computer objects in scoped OUs and a **service connection point (SCP)** configured via *Configure device options* in Entra Connect. Microsoft calls it an interim step towards Entra join.

Check a Windows device's state with `dsregcmd /status`: hybrid joined shows **AzureAdJoined: YES** and **DomainJoined: YES**.

terms.d: BYOD/personal device with a work account added.
Corporate Windows device joined directly to Entra ID.
AD DS-joined device also registered in Entra ID.
Service connection point in AD that tells devices which tenant to register with.

lessons.trap: Personal phones are registered, not joined; hybrid join requires on-premises AD, so cloud-only orgs choose Entra join.
lessons.example: Contoso ships new Windows laptops with Autopilot (Entra joined) while staff phones are Entra registered via Intune.

lessons.title: Managing device join, registration and devices
lessons.short: Control who can join or register devices, cap devices per user, require MFA through Conditional Access, and manage device objects by enabling, disabling or deleting them. Disabling a device blocks Entra authentication and revokes its tokens; deleting can't be undone.
lessons.deep:
**Controlling join and registration** (Device settings):
- Limit **Users may join devices** to a group (default All).
- Turn off **Users may register their devices** to block BYOD registration (this also blocks Intune personal enrolment).
- Require MFA using a Conditional Access policy with the user action **Register or join devices**.
- **Maximum number of devices** per user: default 50.

**Managing device objects** (Devices > All devices):
- **Disable** (Cloud Device Administrator or Intune Administrator): blocks Entra authentication from the device, revokes its Primary Refresh Token and refresh tokens, stops device-based Conditional Access and Windows Hello for Business on it. Reversible.
- **Delete**: removes the object and its details such as **BitLocker recovery keys**; it can't be undone. For Intune-managed devices, wipe or retire in Intune first; Autopilot devices are deleted from Intune first.
- View **BitLocker recovery keys** and **LAPS** passwords (both audited).

**Stale devices**: use the activity timestamp to find inactive devices, disable first, then delete after a grace period.

terms.d: Device-bound token that gives SSO; revoked when a device is disabled.
Device object with no recent activity.
Role that manages device objects and device settings.

lessons.trap: Deleting a device removes its BitLocker keys permanently; the safer first step for a lost or stale device is to disable it.
lessons.example: A laptop is reported lost: the admin disables its device object so it can't get tokens, then retires it in Intune.

lessons.title: Assign, modify and report on licences
lessons.short: Assign licences directly or through group-based licensing, turn off individual service plans, and fix errors such as not enough licences, conflicting service plans or missing usage location. Report on licences in the admin center or with Graph PowerShell.
lessons.deep:
**Direct vs inherited**: a direct licence is assigned to the user; an inherited one comes from **group-based licensing**. Group-based licensing works with security, mail-enabled and Microsoft 365 groups, including dynamic groups, so joiners automatically get licences. It needs a paid licence such as Entra ID P1 (or an Office/Microsoft 365 plan that includes the feature).

**Assigning** (at least **License Administrator**): Billing > Licenses > select product > **Assign**, choose users or groups, and use **Turn apps and services on or off** to disable service plans.

**Rules and errors**
- **Usage location** must be set before licences with location-restricted services apply.
- **Nested groups** aren't supported: only direct members of the licensed group receive licences.
- Errors: **Not enough licences**, **Conflicting service plans** (for example Exchange Online Plan 1 and Plan 2), **Other products depend on this licence**, **Usage location isn't allowed**, **Duplicate proxy addresses**. Fix the cause, then **Reprocess**.
- A direct licence can't be removed while the same licence is inherited; remove the user from the group instead.
- When moving a user between licensed groups, add to the new group first, confirm the licence, then remove from the old one.

**Reporting/automation**: `Get-MgSubscribedSku` (SKUs and consumed units), `Get-MgUser -Property AssignedLicenses,LicenseAssignmentStates`, `Set-MgUserLicense`, `Set-MgGroupLicense`.

terms.d: Licences assigned to a group and inherited by its direct members.
An individual service inside a licence that can be turned off.
Retries licence assignment after an error is fixed.
GUID identifying a licence product.

lessons.trap: Licences on a parent group don't flow to nested groups, and a missing usage location is the classic cause of assignment errors.
lessons.example: Contoso assigns Microsoft 365 E5 to the dynamic group 'All Employees' with Viva Engage turned off.

lessons.title: External collaboration settings
lessons.short: External collaboration settings control what guests can see, who can invite them, whether self-service sign-up is allowed, whether guests can leave on their own, and which domains invitations may go to (allow list or deny list).
lessons.deep:
Find them in **Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings**. Changing them needs a role such as **External Identity Provider Administrator** (or Global Administrator).

**Guest user access** (three levels):
- Same access as members (most inclusive).
- **Limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects** (default).
- Restricted to their own directory objects (most restrictive).

**Guest invite settings** (four levels): anyone including guests can invite (most inclusive, matches the default behaviour); members and specific admin roles; only users in specific admin roles (User Administrator or **Guest Inviter**); no one.

**Enable guest self-service sign-up via user flows**: lets you build user flows so external people sign up for an app themselves.

**External user leave settings**: allow guests to remove themselves; this requires privacy information (privacy contact and statement) in tenant properties.

**Collaboration restrictions**: allow invitations to any domain (default), **deny** invitations to listed domains, or **allow only** listed domains. You choose one mode.

These are tenant-wide B2B settings. Per-organisation inbound/outbound control and MFA trust are set in **cross-tenant access settings**.

terms.d: Role that lets a user invite guests even when invites are limited to admin roles.
Allow list or deny list of domains for B2B invitations.
User flow that lets external users create their own guest account for an app.

lessons.trap: Domain allow/deny lists here control invitations by email domain; blocking access from a specific Entra tenant's users is done in cross-tenant access settings.
lessons.example: Contoso allows invitations only to partner domains fabrikam.com and tailspin.com and limits invites to admins and Guest Inviters.

lessons.title: Invite external users individually or in bulk
lessons.short: Invite a guest from Users > New user > Invite external user, in bulk with a CSV (Bulk invite), or with New-MgInvitation in Microsoft Graph PowerShell. The guest redeems the invitation by email link, a direct app link, or automatic redemption.
lessons.deep:
**Ways to invite**
- **Single invite**: Entra admin center > Users > **New user > Invite external user**; enter the email, optional message, groups and roles.
- **Bulk invite**: Users > Bulk operations > **Bulk invite**; the CSV needs **Email address to invite** and **Redirection url** (for example `https://myapps.microsoft.com`); a custom message is optional (avoid commas). At least **User Administrator** (or Guest Inviter for invitations only).
- **PowerShell / Graph**: `New-MgInvitation -InvitedUserEmailAddress ... -InviteRedirectUrl ... -SendInvitationMessage` (POST `/invitations`).
- Also: adding people to Teams, SharePoint sharing, entitlement management access packages and self-service sign-up flows create guests.

**What gets created**: a user object with **UserType Guest**, a UPN like `john_fabrikam.com#EXT#@contoso.onmicrosoft.com`, and status **Pending acceptance** until redeemed.

**Redemption**: the guest opens the invitation link or a direct link to an app, accepts the consent prompt, and signs in with their identity provider. **Automatic redemption** in cross-tenant access settings can suppress the consent prompt between trusted tenants.

You can **resend** an invitation for pending guests.

terms.d: The guest accepting the invitation and linking their identity.
Marker in a guest's UPN in the resource tenant.
Graph PowerShell cmdlet that invites a B2B user.

lessons.trap: Bulk create makes internal members; only Bulk invite (or New-MgInvitation) makes guests and sends invitations.
lessons.example: A project manager with the Guest Inviter role invites five Fabrikam engineers with a redirect URL to the project's SharePoint site.

lessons.title: Manage external user accounts
lessons.short: Manage guests like other users: groups, apps, licences, sponsors and access reviews. Change UserType between Guest and Member if the relationship changes, and use Reset redemption status when a guest needs a different sign-in identity without losing access.
lessons.deep:
**Key properties**
- **UserType**: Member or Guest; describes the relationship to your organisation, not how they sign in. You can change it.
- **Identities**: the guest's IdP, such as `ExternalAzureAD`, `Microsoft account`, `mail` (email one-time passcode), `google.com` or a SAML/WS-Fed issuer.
- **externalUserState**: `PendingAcceptance` or accepted.
- **Sponsors**: the inviter by default; useful for reviews.

The four categories: **external guest** (most B2B users), **external member** (common in multitenant organisations), **internal guest** (legacy local partner accounts) and **internal member**.

**Reset redemption status** (Helpdesk Administrator is the least-privileged role): when a guest's email or home account changes, reset so they redeem again with the new identity. Object ID, group memberships and app assignments are kept; no need to delete and re-invite. Also available via `New-MgInvitation -ResetRedemption`.

**Other tasks**: block sign-in, delete guests (soft-deleted for 30 days), find inactive guests with **access reviews** or the sign-in activity, and govern them with entitlement management. Guests are hidden from the global address list by default.

terms.d: Member or Guest attribute describing relationship to the organisation.
Lets a guest redeem again with a new identity while keeping access.
User from another tenant with UserType Member.

lessons.trap: Deleting and re-inviting a guest loses group memberships and app assignments; reset redemption status keeps them.
lessons.example: A partner contractor's company was acquired and she has a new email address, so the admin updates her mail property and resets her redemption status.

lessons.title: Cross-tenant access settings
lessons.short: Cross-tenant access settings control B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect with other Microsoft Entra tenants, inbound and outbound, using defaults plus per-organisation overrides. Trust settings can accept a partner's MFA and device claims.
lessons.deep:
**Where**: External Identities > **Cross-tenant access settings**; at least **Security Administrator**.

**Default settings** (apply to all external Entra tenants):
- **B2B collaboration**: inbound and outbound **allowed**; partner MFA and device claims **not trusted**.
- **B2B direct connect**: inbound and outbound **blocked**.

**Organizational settings**: add a partner by tenant ID or domain to override the defaults. You can scope inbound and outbound access to specific users, groups and applications.

**Inbound trust settings**: accept **MFA**, **compliant device** and **Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device** claims from the partner, so your Conditional Access is satisfied without repeat MFA.

**Automatic redemption**: suppresses the consent prompt only when enabled on the home tenant's **outbound** and the resource tenant's **inbound** settings. It is required for cross-tenant synchronization.

**B2B direct connect**: users from the partner get access to **Teams shared channels** without a guest object being created in your tenant. It needs **mutual** configuration (both tenants), and if your policies require MFA you must trust the partner's MFA.

**Microsoft cloud settings** enable B2B collaboration with Azure Government or Microsoft Azure operated by 21Vianet. **Tenant restrictions v2** separately controls which external accounts your users can sign in with on your devices and networks.

Per-user/app scoping and trust need **P1**.

terms.d: External users get a guest object in your tenant.
Mutual trust for Teams shared channels; no guest object.
Accepting a partner's MFA and device claims.
Controls which external tenants your users may sign in to.

lessons.trap: B2B direct connect is blocked by default and must be enabled on both sides; trusting MFA is an inbound setting in the resource tenant.
lessons.example: Contoso adds Fabrikam as an organisation, trusts Fabrikam's MFA inbound, and enables B2B direct connect both ways for a joint Teams shared channel.

lessons.title: Cross-tenant synchronization
lessons.short: Cross-tenant synchronization automatically creates, updates and removes B2B users in a target tenant from a source tenant. It is push-based and configured in the source tenant; the target must allow inbound sync and automatic redemption.
lessons.deep:
**Use it** for organisations with multiple tenants (mergers, subsidiaries) so people in one tenant automatically exist in the others.

**Model**: one-way, push from the **source**. Setup order:
1. **Target**: in cross-tenant access settings for the source, enable inbound **Allow user synchronization into this tenant** and **Automatically redeem invitations**.
2. **Source**: enable outbound **Automatic redemption** for the target.
3. **Source**: create a configuration under **Cross-tenant synchronization > Configurations**, enter the target tenant ID and **Test connection**.
4. Define scope (**Sync only assigned users** recommended), optional scoping filters, review **attribute mappings**.
5. **Provision on demand** to test a user, then **Start provisioning**; check **provisioning logs**.

**Facts**:
- Synced users are created as **external members** by default (can be guests via the userType mapping).
- Only **internal members** of the source are synced; groups sync needs Entra ID Governance or Entra Suite.
- Cycles run roughly every **40 minutes**.
- Removing a user from scope **soft-deletes** them in the target; disabling in the source blocks sign-in in the target.
- Roles: Security Administrator for cross-tenant access settings; **Hybrid Identity Administrator** to configure the sync; Cloud Application Administrator or Application Administrator to assign users.
- Licence: **P1** per synced user in the source tenant; none in the target.

terms.d: Tenant where users live and the sync job is configured.
Tenant that receives the synced B2B users.
Suppresses consent prompts; required on both sides for this sync.

lessons.trap: The sync job is created in the source tenant, not the target; the target only allows inbound sync and auto-redemption.
lessons.example: After acquiring Litware, Contoso pushes all Litware staff into Contoso's tenant as external members so they appear in the Contoso GAL and Teams.

lessons.title: Multitenant organizations
lessons.short: A multitenant organization (MTO) groups the Microsoft Entra tenants you own into one organisational boundary, improving Teams and Viva Engage collaboration across them. It is usually paired with cross-tenant synchronization and needs Entra ID P1.
lessons.deep:
An **MTO** is a tenant group with one **owner** tenant and member tenants, up to **100 active tenants**. Each pair of tenants is still governed by **cross-tenant access settings**.

**Benefits**
- In new Microsoft Teams, users get chat, call and meeting notifications from all MTO tenants and faster tenant switching.
- Viva Engage can work as one network across tenants.
- Users are classified as **multitenant organization members** when they come from another MTO tenant.

**How it is set up**
1. The owner tenant creates the MTO (Microsoft 365 admin center or Entra/Graph) and adds tenants.
2. Each other tenant joins.
3. Users are provisioned across tenants as **external members**, typically by **cross-tenant synchronization** (Microsoft 365 admin center can configure this for you).

**Licensing**: Microsoft Entra ID P1, one per employee per MTO and at least one per tenant.

An MTO doesn't merge tenants. Policies, Conditional Access and admins stay per tenant. For a single tenant with delegated admins, use administrative units instead.

terms.d: A group of tenants your organisation owns, treated as one boundary.
The tenant that creates and manages the MTO.
External member who comes from another tenant in the MTO.

lessons.trap: An MTO doesn't provision users by itself; cross-tenant synchronization (or another provisioning method) creates the users.
lessons.example: A holding company with four subsidiary tenants creates an MTO so staff can find and chat with each other in Teams without switching accounts.

lessons.title: External identity providers incl. SAML and WS-Fed
lessons.short: Guests can sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts, Microsoft accounts, email one-time passcode, Google, Facebook (self-service sign-up only) or a partner's own SAML 2.0 or WS-Federation identity provider. Configuring providers needs at least External Identity Provider Administrator.
lessons.deep:
**Built-in options**
- **Microsoft Entra ID**: always enabled for work or school accounts.
- **Microsoft account (MSA)**.
- **Email one-time passcode (OTP)**: a code by email when no other IdP applies; on by default.
- **Google**: needs an OAuth client ID and secret from Google; works for invitations and sign-up.
- **Facebook**: **self-service sign-up user flows only**, not invitation redemption.

**SAML/WS-Fed IdP federation** lets a partner's own IdP (for example AD FS, Shibboleth or another SAML provider) authenticate their users as guests in your tenant.
You configure (External Identities > All identity providers > **New SAML/WS-Fed IdP**):
- The partner **domain** name(s).
- **Issuer URI** (SAML) or entity ID (WS-Fed).
- **Passive authentication endpoint** (https only).
- The token-signing **certificate**, or better, a **metadata URL** so certificates renew automatically.

DNS rule: if the passive endpoint isn't on the partner's domain, the partner adds a TXT record `DirectFedAuthUrl=<endpoint>`.
Required claims include a persistent **NameID** and the **emailaddress** claim (SAML), or **ImmutableID** and email (WS-Fed). Allow 5-10 minutes before testing. Changing the IdP for already-redeemed guests requires resetting redemption status.

WS-Fed is tested with AD FS and Shibboleth.

terms.d: B2B trust with a partner's own identity provider.
Unique identifier of the partner IdP in the token.
Partner IdP URL where users are redirected to sign in.
Guests sign in with a code emailed to them.

lessons.trap: Facebook can't be used to redeem invitations, and a SAML/WS-Fed setup without a metadata URL won't auto-renew the signing certificate.
lessons.example: Contoso federates with Fabrikam's AD FS so Fabrikam guests sign in with their own Fabrikam passwords and MFA.

lessons.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: architecture and install
lessons.short: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync is the on-premises sync server that copies users, groups, contacts and devices from AD DS to Microsoft Entra ID. It also configures sign-in (PHS, PTA, federation), writeback and hybrid join, and supports a staging-mode server for failover.
lessons.deep:
**What it does**: a Windows service on a domain-joined server that reads AD DS forests through connectors, joins objects in a **metaverse**, and exports them to Entra ID. Optional features: **password hash sync**, **password writeback**, **group writeback**, **device options** (hybrid join), **Exchange hybrid** attributes, directory extensions.

**Install requirements**
- Windows Server with a full GUI (Server Core isn't supported), domain-joined, treated as a **Tier 0** asset. TLS 1.2 required.
- SQL Server Express LocalDB by default: **10 GB, about 100,000 objects**; use full SQL Server for more.
- **Express settings** need an on-premises **Enterprise Admin** account, plus a **Global Administrator or Hybrid Identity Administrator** (assigned directly, not through a group) in Entra ID.
- Only **one sync engine per SQL instance**.

**High availability**: only one server actively exports. A second server in **staging mode** imports and synchronises but doesn't export; switch it to active if the primary fails.

**Topology**: supports multiple connected forests and merging attributes from several forests. Mandatory version updates apply, so keep it current.

terms.d: Central sync store where connector space objects are joined.
Standby sync server that imports and syncs but doesn't export.
Default install for single forest with PHS; needs Enterprise Admin.

lessons.trap: Two active Connect Sync servers for one tenant isn't supported; the second server must be in staging mode.
lessons.example: Contoso installs Entra Connect on SYNC01 and a staging-mode server SYNC02 in another site for disaster recovery.

lessons.title: Connect Sync operations: scheduler and filtering
lessons.short: Connect Sync runs a delta sync every 30 minutes by default. Use Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta for an immediate sync, Initial after configuration changes, and disable the scheduler while changing filtering or sync rules.
lessons.deep:
**Scheduler** (ADSync PowerShell module on the sync server):
- `Get-ADSyncScheduler` shows the interval (default **30 minutes**), whether sync and maintenance are enabled, and `StagingModeEnabled`.
- `Set-ADSyncScheduler -SyncCycleEnabled $false` before making changes; set it back to `$true` afterwards.
- `Set-ADSyncScheduler -CustomizedSyncCycleInterval 01:00:00` changes the interval.
- `Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta` runs delta import, delta sync and export now; `-PolicyType Initial` runs a full import and full sync (slow; needed after many configuration changes).

**Filtering** decides which objects reach Entra ID:
- **Domain** and **OU-based** filtering (in the wizard).
- **Attribute-based** filtering with custom sync rules in the Synchronization Rules Editor.
- **Group-based** filtering, intended for pilots only.

After changing filtering, a **full import** (and full sync) is usually needed. Watch for accidental deletes: the **prevent accidental deletes** feature stops exports deleting more than 500 objects by default.

Troubleshoot with the **Synchronization Service Manager**, the Entra Connect Health sync errors page and the provisioning or audit logs.

terms.d: Processes only changes since the last run.
Re-reads all objects; used after rule or filtering changes.
Selects which AD organizational units are synced.
Stops an export that would delete more than a threshold of objects.

lessons.trap: Expect Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta for 'sync this change now', not Initial; and disable the scheduler before editing rules.
lessons.example: An admin adds a new OU to the sync scope, then runs an initial sync so the OU's users appear in Entra ID.

lessons.title: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
lessons.short: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync uses lightweight provisioning agents on-premises with configuration in the cloud. Multiple active agents give high availability, and it supports disconnected forests, but it lacks some Connect Sync features such as PTA configuration and advanced sync rules.
lessons.deep:
**Architecture**: the **Microsoft Entra provisioning agent** installs on domain-joined servers (or DCs) and keeps an outbound connection to Entra ID. Configuration, scheduling and monitoring are in the **Microsoft Entra admin center**; sync runs about every **2 minutes**. The agent runs as a **gMSA** (`provAgentgMSA$`). Install with a **Hybrid Identity Administrator** account; Microsoft recommends **three active agents** for HA.

**Cloud Sync strengths**
- **Disconnected forests** (for example after a merger with no trust).
- **Multiple active agents** with automatic failover.
- **Provision on demand** for testing.
- **Group provisioning to AD** (cloud groups written to AD DS).
- PHS, password writeback, Exchange hybrid attributes, device sync for hybrid join, OU scoping.

**Connect Sync still needed for**
- **Pass-through authentication** and **AD FS** configuration.
- **Advanced custom sync rules**, full attribute-value filtering and merging attributes from several forests.
- Very large tenants: Cloud Sync supports up to **150,000 objects per domain** and groups up to **50,000 members**.

Both can run side by side for different scopes (for example Cloud Sync for a newly acquired forest) as long as an object is synced by only one.

terms.d: Lightweight on-premises agent used by Cloud Sync.
AD forest without trust to other forests.
Group managed service account the agent runs as.

lessons.trap: If the scenario needs PTA, custom sync rules or merging attributes across forests, the answer is Connect Sync, not Cloud Sync.
lessons.example: After acquiring a company with an untrusted AD forest, Contoso deploys three Cloud Sync agents there instead of building a forest trust.

lessons.title: Password hash synchronization
lessons.short: Password hash synchronization (PHS) syncs a hash of the AD password hash to Microsoft Entra ID so users sign in with the same password, authenticated in the cloud. It is the simplest method, keeps working if on-premises is down, and enables leaked credential detection.
lessons.deep:
**How it works**: the sync agent pulls the MD4-based password hash from a DC, adds a per-user **salt**, and runs **PBKDF2 (HMAC-SHA256, 1,000 iterations)** before sending it over TLS. The original hash is never sent and the plaintext is never known. Changes sync roughly **every 2 minutes**, separate from the 30-minute object sync.

**Why Microsoft recommends PHS**
- Cloud authentication with no extra on-premises servers.
- Users can still sign in if AD DS or the sync server is down.
- Enables **leaked credentials** detection in Microsoft Entra ID Protection.
- Can be enabled as a **backup** alongside PTA or federation.

**Behaviour to know**
- By default synced users' cloud passwords are set to **never expire**, because AD enforces expiry. Turn on `CloudPasswordPolicyForPasswordSyncedUsersEnabled` to apply Entra's policy.
- 'User must change password at next logon' only syncs with `UserForcePasswordChangeOnLogonEnabled` (use with SSPR and password writeback).
- An account disabled in AD is disabled in Entra at the next sync, but an **expired** AD account (accountExpires) isn't synced.
- On-premises account lockout and logon hours aren't evaluated at cloud sign-in; Entra **smart lockout** protects cloud sign-ins.

Enable it in the Entra Connect wizard (**Optional features** or **Change user sign-in**) or Cloud Sync.

terms.d: Password hash synchronization: cloud authentication using a synced hash.
ID Protection risk detection that requires PHS.
Entra ID lockout that blocks brute-force attempts in the cloud.

lessons.trap: Leaked credentials detection needs PHS even when users sign in with PTA or federation, so enable PHS as well.
lessons.example: Contoso uses PTA but also enables PHS so ID Protection flags leaked passwords and sign-in can fall back to PHS in a disaster.

lessons.title: Pass-through authentication
lessons.short: Pass-through authentication (PTA) validates passwords directly against on-premises AD DS through lightweight agents that make outbound-only connections. Choose it when on-premises account states, password policies and sign-in hours must be enforced at sign-in, and no password hash may go to the cloud.
lessons.deep:
**Flow**: the user enters a password at Entra ID, which places the encrypted request on a queue; an on-premises **authentication agent** picks it up, validates against a DC and returns the result. No password is stored in the cloud.

**Agents**
- Install on domain-joined Windows Server 2016 or later (not Server Core). The first agent is installed with Entra Connect.
- **Outbound only**: port **443** for traffic and **80** for certificate revocation lists. No inbound ports or perimeter network needed.
- Microsoft recommends **at least three agents** for high availability.
- Registering agents needs a **Hybrid Identity Administrator** account (ideally cloud-only).

**Why choose PTA**: on-premises policies such as **disabled, locked-out or expired accounts, password expiry and logon hours** apply immediately at sign-in. Some organisations' security rules forbid sending any password hash to the cloud.

**Considerations**
- If all agents are unreachable, sign-in fails and there is no automatic failover, so enable **PHS as a backup** that you switch to manually in Entra Connect (it also gives leaked credentials detection).
- Pair with **Seamless SSO** for silent sign-in on domain-joined devices.
- Configured only with **Connect Sync**, not Cloud Sync.
- Free; no paid Entra licence.

terms.d: Pass-through authentication; validates passwords against on-premises AD.
On-premises PTA service that validates sign-in requests.
Agent initiates all connections; no inbound firewall rules.

lessons.trap: PTA is the answer when on-premises account policies like logon hours must apply in real time; PHS doesn't evaluate them at sign-in.
lessons.example: A bank whose policy forbids storing password hashes in the cloud deploys three PTA agents across two datacentres.

lessons.title: Seamless single sign-on (SSO)
lessons.short: Seamless SSO signs users on domain-joined devices inside the corporate network into Microsoft Entra ID automatically using Kerberos. It works with PHS or PTA, not AD FS, and creates the AZUREADSSOACC computer account whose key you should roll over every 30 days.
lessons.deep:
**How it works**: when enabled (Entra Connect wizard or PowerShell), a computer account **AZUREADSSOACC** is created in each AD forest. Browsers on domain-joined devices request a Kerberos ticket for Entra ID, which decrypts it with the shared key and signs the user in without a password prompt.

**Requirements and setup**
- Works with **PHS** or **PTA**; not used with AD FS (which has its own SSO).
- Device must be **domain-joined** and have line of sight to a DC.
- Add `https://autologon.microsoftazuread-sso.com` to the browsers' **Local intranet zone** via Group Policy.
- Supported browsers include Edge, Chrome and (with extra configuration) Firefox and Safari.

**When it's used**: mainly for **Windows 7/8.1** and non-Entra-joined scenarios. **Windows 10/11 Entra joined or hybrid joined** devices use the **Primary Refresh Token (PRT)** for SSO instead.

**Maintenance**: protect AZUREADSSOACC like a DC object and **roll over its Kerberos decryption key at least every 30 days** (`Update-AzureADSSOForest`).

Seamless SSO is opportunistic: if it fails, users just see the normal sign-in page. It is free and needs no paid licence.

terms.d: Kerberos-based silent sign-in for domain-joined devices on the corporate network.
AD computer account holding the Seamless SSO Kerberos key.
Browser zone that must include the autologon URL.

lessons.trap: Seamless SSO doesn't work with AD FS sign-in, and modern Windows 10/11 joined devices rely on PRT rather than Seamless SSO.
lessons.example: Contoso enables PTA with Seamless SSO and pushes the autologon URL to the intranet zone so office users reach Microsoft 365 without typing a password.

lessons.title: Migrate authentication from AD FS
lessons.short: Moving from AD FS to cloud authentication (PHS recommended, or PTA) reduces infrastructure and risk. Test with staged rollout groups, then convert federated domains to managed with Entra Connect or Update-MgDomain, and finally decommission AD FS.
lessons.deep:
**Plan**: document the current federation settings (`Get-MgDomainFederationConfiguration`), back up AD FS, review Conditional Access and MFA behaviour, prepare SSO (PRT for Windows 10/11, Seamless SSO for older Windows), and plan rollback.

**Staged rollout** (Hybrid Identity Administrator): lets selected **security groups** use PHS, PTA or certificate-based authentication while the domain **stays federated**.
- Up to **10 groups per feature**; **nested and dynamic groups aren't supported**; adding a group with more than 200 users at once can time out.
- Only **synced** users are in scope; apps sending `domain_hint` still go to federation.
- PHS must be enabled and fully synced before testing PHS.

**Cut over**
- **Option A**: if AD FS was configured by Entra Connect, use **Change user sign-in** in the wizard to switch to PHS or PTA; it converts the domains.
- **Option B**: otherwise, enable PHS/PTA in Entra Connect, then run `Update-MgDomain -DomainId contoso.com -AuthenticationType Managed` per domain.
- Conversion can take up to an hour; do it in a maintenance window.

**After**: confirm sign-ins with Connect Health/sign-in logs, turn off staged rollout, remove the Microsoft 365 relying party trust, and keep AD FS only if it still serves other apps.

terms.d: Test cloud authentication for selected groups while the domain stays federated.
Domain that authenticates in Entra ID (PHS/PTA).
Graph PowerShell cmdlet used to convert a domain to Managed.

lessons.trap: Staged rollout doesn't convert the domain; you still have to switch it to Managed, and dynamic or nested groups can't be used.
lessons.example: Contoso adds a 50-user pilot security group to staged rollout for PHS, validates for two weeks, then converts contoso.com to Managed.

lessons.title: Migrate apps from AD FS to Entra ID
lessons.short: Apps that use AD FS relying party trusts can move to Microsoft Entra ID as enterprise applications (SAML, WS-Fed, OIDC) or app registrations. Use the AD FS application activity report to find apps and check migration readiness.
lessons.deep:
**Discover**: the **AD FS application activity** report (Entra ID > Enterprise applications > Usage & insights) uses **Microsoft Entra Connect Health for AD FS** data to list relying parties, their sign-in counts and a **migration readiness** status with the claim rules that need attention.

**Move each app**
- **SAML 2.0 / WS-Fed SaaS apps**: add from the **gallery** or as a non-gallery enterprise application and configure SAML-based SSO (identifier, reply URL, claims).
- **OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect line-of-business apps**: create an **app registration**.
- **Legacy header or Kerberos apps**: publish with **Microsoft Entra Application Proxy** (or Private Access) or a secure hybrid access partner.
- Re-create claim rules as Entra **claims mapping** and access rules as **Conditional Access**.

**Stages**: production app on AD FS → (optional) test instance against a test tenant → test instance against production tenant → production app against Entra ID.

Migrate modern-protocol apps first. When all relying parties have moved and the domains are managed, decommission the AD FS farm and Web Application Proxy servers.

terms.d: AD FS configuration for an app that trusts AD FS tokens.
Entra report listing AD FS apps and migration readiness.
Configuring which claims Entra ID puts in an app's token.

lessons.trap: The AD FS application activity report needs Connect Health for AD FS agents; without them, no data appears.
lessons.example: The report shows 23 relying parties; 18 are 'Ready', so Contoso adds them as enterprise apps and plans custom claims for the rest.

lessons.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health
lessons.short: Microsoft Entra Connect Health monitors hybrid identity through agents for Entra Connect Sync, AD FS and AD DS, giving alerts, sync error reports, performance data and AD FS usage analytics. It needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.
lessons.deep:
**Agents**
- **Connect Health for sync**: installed automatically with Entra Connect; shows sync latency, alerts and **sync errors** (for example duplicate attributes).
- **Connect Health for AD FS**: alerts, **usage analytics**, performance monitoring, the **Bad password attempts** report (top 50 users) and the **Risky IP** report. Usage analytics needs **AD FS auditing** enabled (`Set-AdfsProperties -AuditLevel Verbose` plus the Generate security audits right).
- **Connect Health for AD DS**: DC health, replication and authentication monitoring.

**Licensing**: P1 or P2. The first agent needs 1 licence and **each additional agent needs 25 more** (for example 2 agents = 26 licences). Licences don't have to be assigned to particular users.

**Access**: Global Administrators always have full access; **Hybrid Identity Administrators** are Owner by default. You can grant **Owner**, **Contributor** or **Reader** for all or specific service instances.

**Notifications**: alert emails go to Global Administrators by default, and you can add other recipients. Agents use outbound connections; if Azure is unreachable they buffer data locally.

terms.d: Monitoring agent for Sync, AD FS or AD DS.
AD FS authentication traffic analysis; needs AD FS auditing.
AD FS report of IPs with many failed sign-ins.

lessons.trap: Connect Health licensing is 1 licence for the first agent plus 25 for each additional agent, not one per server user.
lessons.example: An alert from Connect Health warns Contoso that the sync server hasn't exported for three hours, so they fail over to the staging server.

lessons.title: Planning authentication
lessons.short: Plan authentication by choosing which methods users may register and use in the **Authentication methods policy**, moving users toward passwordless and phishing-resistant methods, and deciding between security defaults and Conditional Access.
lessons.deep:
Authentication planning starts with *what proves who you are*. Methods range from weak (password, SMS) to phishing-resistant (passkeys/FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, multifactor certificate-based authentication).

**Authentication methods policy** (Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies) is now the single place to enable each method and scope it to groups. The legacy per-user MFA and SSPR method settings stopped being manageable after **30 September 2025**; tenants migrate through the states **Migration in progress** (both policies honoured) and **Migration complete** (only the Authentication methods policy is used; legacy settings are greyed out except SSPR security questions).

**System-preferred MFA** prompts users with the strongest method they have registered. *Enabled* affects only the second factor; *Microsoft managed* (the default) also affects the first factor.

Baseline choice:
- **Security defaults**: free, on/off only, requires Microsoft Authenticator registration, MFA for admins, blocks legacy authentication.
- **Conditional Access**: needs Entra ID P1, fully customisable; you must turn security defaults off to use it.

The **Authentication Policy Administrator** role manages the Authentication methods policy.

terms.d: Tenant policy that enables each sign-in method and targets it to users or groups.
State where only the Authentication methods policy governs MFA and SSPR methods.
Prompts the user for their most secure registered method.
Free, non-configurable baseline: MFA registration, admin MFA, legacy auth blocked.

lessons.trap: Exams expect the Authentication methods policy as the place to enable methods; answers pointing to the legacy MFA service settings page are outdated.
lessons.example: Contoso has P1 licences and wants different MFA rules per department, so it disables security defaults, migrates methods to the Authentication methods policy and builds Conditional Access policies.

lessons.title: Certificate-based auth and Temporary Access Pass
lessons.short: **Certificate-based authentication (CBA)** lets users sign in with an X.509 certificate validated against CAs you upload to Entra ID. A **Temporary Access Pass (TAP)** is a time-limited passcode used to onboard or recover passwordless methods.
lessons.deep:
**CBA** removes the need for AD FS when using smart cards. Setup order: upload trusted CAs to the **PKI-based trust store** (with a CRL URL), enable CBA for a group in the Authentication methods policy, set the **authentication binding**, set the **username binding**, then test.
- *Authentication binding* sets protection level: the default is **single-factor**; rules by **issuer** or **policy OID** can mark certificates **multifactor**. A policy OID rule beats an issuer rule.
- *Username binding* maps a certificate field to a user attribute. Default: SAN **PrincipalName** to `userPrincipalName`. **High-affinity** bindings (SKI, SHA1PublicKey, IssuerAndSerialNumber) map to `certificateUserIds`.
- If no CRL is configured, revocation is **not** checked.
- Privileged Authentication Administrator manages the trust store; Authentication Policy Administrator enables CBA.

**TAP** defaults: lifetime 1 hour (min/max 1-8 hours by default, range 10 minutes-30 days), length 8 (8-48), multi-use unless *one-time* is set. A one-time TAP used to register a passwordless method must finish within 10 minutes. TAP doesn't replace the password, and doesn't work with the NPS extension or AD FS adapter. Authentication Administrators create TAPs for non-admins; **Privileged Authentication Administrators** for admins.

terms.d: Where trusted root/intermediate CAs and their CRL URLs are uploaded for CBA.
Rule deciding whether a certificate counts as single-factor or multifactor.
Mapping from a certificate field to a user attribute to find the account.
Time-limited passcode that satisfies strong auth for onboarding methods.

lessons.trap: A common trap is assuming CBA is multifactor by default; it is single-factor until an authentication binding rule says otherwise.
lessons.example: New hires receive a one-time TAP valid for 8 hours on day one, sign in to Security info and register a passkey within 10 minutes.

lessons.title: Microsoft Authenticator and passkeys (FIDO2)
lessons.short: **Microsoft Authenticator** provides push notifications with **number matching**, passwordless phone sign-in and passkeys. **Passkeys (FIDO2)** are phishing-resistant credentials; Entra ID supports device-bound and synced passkeys controlled through passkey profiles.
lessons.deep:
**Microsoft Authenticator** settings live under Authentication methods > Microsoft Authenticator. **Authentication mode** is *Any* (push and passwordless phone sign-in) or *Push* (no passwordless). **Number matching** is always on for push notifications and can't be disabled. Admins can add **additional context**: show the **application name** and **geographic location** in notifications, which helps users spot MFA-fatigue attacks.

**Passkeys (FIDO2)** use public-key cryptography bound to the sign-in origin, so they resist phishing. Available in all Entra ID editions.
- **Device-bound** passkeys keep the private key on one device (FIDO2 security keys, passkeys in Authenticator).
- **Synced** passkeys are stored in a provider such as iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager; they don't support attestation.
- **Passkey profiles** (up to three, opt-in can't be undone) set *Enforce attestation*, allowed passkey types and **key restrictions** (allow or block by **AAGUID**, applied at registration and sign-in).
- *Allow self-service set up* = No stops users registering in Security info.
- Users must have completed MFA in the last **five minutes** to register a passkey. Guest/B2B users aren't supported.

terms.d: User types the number shown on the sign-in screen into Authenticator to approve.
Identifier of an authenticator make/model, used in key restriction lists.
Proof of an authenticator's make and model checked at registration.
Passkey stored and synced by a cloud provider; not attestable.

lessons.trap: Distractors often claim number matching can be turned off per group; it can't for Authenticator push.
lessons.example: Fabrikam allows only two approved security-key models by adding their AAGUIDs to an allow list in the passkey profile with attestation enforced.

lessons.title: Tenant-wide MFA settings
lessons.short: Tenant-wide MFA settings include **Report suspicious activity**, OATH token management, phone call settings, the legacy **trusted IPs** and **remember MFA** options, plus system-preferred authentication. Most now live in the Authentication methods policy settings.
lessons.deep:
Several MFA settings apply to the whole tenant:
- **Report suspicious activity** (Authentication methods > Settings) replaced the legacy *fraud alert*, *block/unblock users* and *notifications* features (removed March 2025). When a user reports an unrecognised MFA prompt, the user is set to **high user risk**, so risk-based Conditional Access (P2) can act. The default reporting code for voice calls is 0.
- **OATH tokens**: TOTP (30 or 60 second) hardware tokens and software apps; up to **5** per user.
- **Phone call settings**: custom caller ID must be a US number.
- **Legacy MFA service settings**: *trusted IPs* (P1, up to 50 public ranges, IPv4) and *remember MFA on trusted devices*. Microsoft recommends Conditional Access named locations and **sign-in frequency** instead; remember MFA conflicts with sign-in frequency and should be disabled first.
- **System-preferred authentication** and Authenticator *additional context* are also tenant-level choices.

Revoking a user's sessions also clears any remember-MFA trust.

terms.d: Lets users flag unexpected MFA prompts; raises user risk to high.
TOTP code generator (hardware or software) used as an MFA method.
