Templates include **Sign-ins using legacy authentication**, **Conditional Access gap analyzer**, **Authentication prompts analysis**, **Sensitive Operations Report**, **Cross-tenant access activity** and **Risk analysis**.
lessons.deep:
Open **Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Workbooks**. Tabs: **Workbooks** (saved), **Public Templates**, **My Templates**. Workbooks query a **Log Analytics workspace**, so you need diagnostic settings sending logs there first and an **Entra ID P1** tenant.

Roles: read Entra data with **Reports Reader**, Security Reader or Global Reader; read the workspace with **Log Analytics Reader** or Monitoring Reader; edit with Log Analytics Contributor or Monitoring Contributor; creating the diagnostic setting needs Security Administrator.

Useful templates:
- **Sign-ins using legacy authentication**: who still uses basic/legacy protocols before you block them.
- **Conditional Access gap analyzer**: sign-ins not covered by policies.
- **Multifactor authentication gaps** and **Authentication prompts analysis**: MFA coverage and prompt fatigue.
- **Sensitive Operations Report**: risky changes such as new credentials on apps.
- **Cross-tenant access activity**: inbound/outbound B2B use.
- **Risk analysis**: ID Protection trends.
Governance workbooks such as **Access Package Activity** use audit data too.

You can edit a template, save it to a resource group, or build one with **+ New**. Also use built-in **Usage & insights** reports and the **Recommendations** page.

terms.d: Interactive Azure Monitor report built on Log Analytics data.
Microsoft-provided workbook you can open and customise.
Basic-auth protocols that can't do MFA.

lessons.trap: Workbooks show nothing until logs are sent to a Log Analytics workspace with diagnostic settings.
lessons.example: Before blocking legacy auth, the admin uses the legacy authentication workbook to find three printers still using SMTP basic auth.

lessons.title: Identity Secure Score
lessons.short: **Identity Secure Score** is a percentage showing how well the tenant follows Microsoft's identity security recommendations. It's recalculated every **24 hours** and is the identity part of **Microsoft Secure Score**.
lessons.deep:
Find it in **Entra admin center > Entra ID > Identity Secure Score** (or **Overview > Recommendations** filtered to Security); the full Microsoft Secure Score is in the **Microsoft Defender portal**. Viewing requires at least **Global Reader**.

Scoring: each **improvement action** carries points. Some are binary (setting on or off); others are partial, scored by the share of users covered (e.g. MFA for 50 of 100 admins earns half the points). Actions marked **[Not Scored]** improve security but add no points. Typical actions: require MFA for administrative roles, block legacy authentication, designate more than one Global Administrator, enable self-service password reset, protect all users with user risk and sign-in risk policies, use least-privileged roles.

**Statuses** you can set on an action: **To address**, **Planned**, **Risk accepted** (no points), **Resolved through third party** and **Resolved through alternate mitigation** (points awarded but unverified), and **Ignored**. Score updates take up to a day. It's available to all tenants, though some actions need paid licences. The score measures adoption of controls, not breach probability.

terms.d: Recommendation with points toward the score.
Status for an action you won't do; earns no points.
Overall score across identity, data, devices, apps and infrastructure.

lessons.trap: Marking an action Risk accepted removes it from the to-do list but earns no points; third-party and alternate mitigation statuses do award points.
lessons.example: The score is 48%; requiring MFA for admin roles and blocking legacy authentication lift it within a day.

questions.stem: Tier-1 support staff must reset passwords for non-administrator users and invalidate their refresh tokens. They must not create users, manage groups or assign licences. Which built-in role should you assign?
options: User Administrator
License Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explain: Helpdesk Administrator resets passwords and invalidates refresh tokens for non-admins without user-creation rights. User Administrator also creates users and manages groups (too broad). License Administrator only manages licences. Privileged Role Administrator manages role assignments.

questions.stem: You try to assign the Groups Administrator role to an existing assigned security group named IT-Ops, but the group isn't offered in the role assignment pane. What should you do?
options: Create a new security group with 'Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group' set to Yes
Edit IT-Ops and turn on 'Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group'
Convert IT-Ops to a Microsoft 365 group
Change IT-Ops to Dynamic user membership
questions.explain: isAssignableToRole can only be set when a group is created, so a new role-assignable group is required. It can't be enabled on an existing group. Group type conversion doesn't help, and role-assignable groups can't use dynamic membership.

questions.stem: For each statement about role-assignable groups, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A role-assignable group can use a dynamic membership rule.
You can add another group as a member of a role-assignable group.
A tenant can have up to 500 role-assignable groups.

questions.explain: Role-assignable groups must use Assigned membership to prevent unintended elevation, and nesting a group inside one isn't supported. The documented limit is 500 role-assignable groups per tenant.

questions.stem: What is the minimum licence required for each user who is assigned a custom Microsoft Entra role?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Free
Microsoft Entra ID P1
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Entra Suite
questions.explain: Custom roles require Microsoft Entra ID P1 for every assignee; built-in roles are available with Free. Entra ID Governance and Entra Suite include more features, but they aren't the minimum.

questions.stem: You need a custom Microsoft Entra role that only lets holders update app registration credentials. Complete the Microsoft Graph PowerShell command.
options: New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleDefinition
New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment
New-MgDirectoryRole
New-MgApplication
questions.explain: New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleDefinition creates the custom role definition from rolePermissions. ...RoleAssignment assigns an existing role to a principal. New-MgDirectoryRole activates a built-in role template (legacy API), and New-MgApplication creates an app registration.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about custom Microsoft Entra roles are true? Select TWO.
options: Permissions are chosen from a preset list, the same permissions used by built-in roles
Any Microsoft Graph API permission can be added to a custom role
You can edit a built-in role to add the permissions you need
Creating custom roles requires at least the Privileged Role Administrator role
Custom roles can be assigned without any paid licence
questions.explain: Custom roles are built from preset directory permissions that built-in roles also use, and creating them needs at least Privileged Role Administrator. Graph API permissions are an app consent concept, built-in roles can't be edited, and custom role assignees need P1.

questions.case: Northwind University has one Microsoft Entra tenant with users for the Faculty of Arts and the Faculty of Science. Each faculty has its own IT team. Each team must reset passwords only for its own faculty's students and staff. Administrative effort should be minimal and the tenant must stay single.
questions.stem: What should you implement?
options: Dynamic groups for each faculty with the IT team members as group owners
A custom role for each faculty that includes password reset permissions
PIM for Groups with an approval workflow per faculty
An administrative unit per faculty with Helpdesk Administrator assigned at the administrative unit scope
questions.explain: Administrative units scope a role to a subset of users, so each team only manages its faculty. Group owners manage membership, not passwords. A custom role still needs a scope; on its own it is tenant-wide. PIM controls when a role is active, not which users it covers.

questions.stem: For each statement about administrative units, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An administrative unit can be nested inside another administrative unit.
A user with a role scoped to an administrative unit can still browse users outside it using default user permissions.
The Global Administrator role can be assigned at administrative unit scope.

questions.explain: Administrative units can't be nested. They limit management permissions only, so default read access to the directory remains. Global Administrator is tenant-wide and can't be scoped to an administrative unit.

questions.stem: You want an administrative unit's membership to update automatically by rule. Which object types can be added to an administrative unit by a dynamic membership rule?
options: Users only
Users and devices
Users, groups and devices
Groups only
questions.explain: Dynamic membership for administrative units supports users and devices. Groups can be added to an administrative unit manually but not by dynamic rule.

questions.stem: You must assign the User Administrator role to a user, scoped only to the administrative unit stored in $auId. Complete the command.
options: "/administrativeUnits/$auId"
"/groups/$auId"
"/tenants/$auId"
questions.explain: An administrative unit scope is expressed as /administrativeUnits/{id}. "/" means tenant-wide. /groups/... is not how AU scopes are written, and /tenants/ isn't a valid directory scope here.

questions.case: Contoso has 12 tenant-wide User Administrators. Security requires that the accounts of the CEO, CFO and board members can be modified only by a three-person Executive Support team. The tenant-wide administrators must keep their current role assignments for all other users.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Create a standard administrative unit for the executives and assign the Executive Support team User Administrator on it
Add the executives to a role-assignable group owned by the Executive Support team
Create a restricted management administrative unit for the executives and assign the Executive Support team User Administrator scoped to it
Require PIM approval from the Executive Support team for all User Administrator activations
questions.explain: A restricted management administrative unit blocks tenant-scoped admins from changing its members, so only admins assigned at its scope can. A standard AU adds the team but doesn't block the other 12 admins. Group ownership and PIM approval don't restrict which users tenant admins can modify.

questions.stem: For each statement about restricted management administrative units, select Yes if true.

statements.s: You can turn on restricted management for an existing administrative unit.
A Global Administrator without a role at the unit's scope can change the properties of users in the unit.
Security groups can be members, but Microsoft 365 groups can't.

questions.explain: Restricted management is set at creation and can't be changed later. Global Administrators can manage the unit itself, but can't modify its members unless they assign themselves a scoped role. Users, devices and security groups are supported; Microsoft 365 groups aren't.

questions.stem: Ana has Helpdesk Administrator at tenant scope and User Administrator scoped to the Sales administrative unit. Raj is a non-admin Marketing user who isn't in any administrative unit. Which action can Ana perform on Raj?
options: Reset Raj's password
Delete Raj's account
Assign Raj a Microsoft 365 licence
Change Raj's user principal name
questions.explain: Permissions combine, but each is limited by scope. Tenant-scoped Helpdesk Administrator lets Ana reset Raj's password. Deleting, licensing and changing the UPN need User Administrator rights, and Ana has those only for Sales AU members.

questions.stem: You need to see every Microsoft Entra role a user holds, the scope of each, and whether it was assigned directly or through a group. Where should you look?
options: The user's sign-in logs
The user's Assigned roles page
Identity Secure Score
The user's Licenses page
questions.explain: The Assigned roles page lists each role, its scope and the assignment path (direct or group), plus eligible assignments with PIM. Sign-in logs show authentication events, Secure Score shows recommendations, and Licenses shows products.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about evaluating effective Microsoft Entra role permissions are true? Select TWO.
options: Permissions from all of a user's active role assignments are combined
A PIM-eligible assignment grants no permissions until it is activated
A role scoped to an administrative unit lets the holder rename or delete that administrative unit
A role assigned to a group gives the group's members rights over the group's other members only
questions.explain: Active assignments add together, and eligible PIM roles grant nothing until activated. A container-scoped role applies to the objects inside the unit, not the unit object. A role assigned to a role-assignable group grants its members that role at the assignment's scope, not just over each other.

questions.stem: You add contoso.com as a custom domain in Microsoft Entra ID. Which DNS record type can you create at the registrar to verify ownership?
options: CNAME
SRV
TXT
PTR
questions.explain: Domain verification uses a TXT record (or an MX record) with the value Microsoft Entra ID provides. CNAME and SRV records are used for service discovery after verification, and PTR records are reverse lookups.

questions.stem: Contoso acquired Tailspin. tailspin.com is verified in Tailspin's old Microsoft Entra tenant, and you need it verified in Contoso's tenant. What must happen first?
options: Add a second TXT record so both tenants can verify the domain
Federate tailspin.com with Contoso's tenant
Set tailspin.com as the primary domain in Contoso's tenant
Remove tailspin.com, and all references to it, from Tailspin's tenant
questions.explain: A domain can be verified in only one directory, so it must be removed from the old tenant (after removing UPNs, addresses and other references) before it can be verified in Contoso. Extra TXT records or federation don't bypass that, and an unverified domain can't be made primary.

questions.stem: You want new users to sign in as name@fabrikam.com. Put the steps in order.
options: Add fabrikam.com under Domain names in the Microsoft Entra admin center
Create the TXT record shown by Microsoft Entra ID at the DNS registrar
Select Verify for fabrikam.com
Set fabrikam.com as the primary domain
questions.explain: You add the domain to get the verification values, publish the TXT record, then verify. Only a verified domain can be made primary so new users default to it.

questions.stem: Users who open https://myapps.microsoft.com see the default Microsoft sign-in page until they enter their username. You want Contoso branding on the first screen. What should you do?
options: Add a browser language customization for English
Share the URL with the parameter whr=contoso.com
Upload a larger banner logo
Assign users Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences
questions.explain: Multitenant Microsoft sites don't know the tenant until the username is entered. A home realm hint (whr=contoso.com) identifies the tenant up front so branding shows immediately. Language variants, logos and licences don't change when the tenant is identified.

questions.stem: For each statement about company branding, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Organizational Branding Administrator is the least-privileged role that can configure company branding.
Sign-in page text can contain up to 1,024 characters.
B2B guests signing in to your tenant see your tenant's branding instead of their home tenant's branding.

questions.explain: Organizational Branding Administrator is the minimum role, and sign-in page text allows 1,024 characters. B2B guests from other Entra tenants see their home tenant's branding.

questions.stem: A Global Administrator has no access to an Azure subscription whose only Owner left the company. Which tenant setting lets the Global Administrator regain access?
options: Access management for Azure resources in the tenant properties
Restrict access to Microsoft Entra admin center in user settings
Security defaults
Technical contact in the tenant properties
questions.explain: Setting Access management for Azure resources to Yes grants the Global Administrator User Access Administrator at Azure root scope, so they can fix role assignments. The other settings don't grant any Azure RBAC rights.

questions.stem: You must stop non-admin users from creating app registrations and security groups. Users with admin roles must keep these abilities. Which TWO settings should you change? Select TWO.
options: Set 'Users can register applications' to No
Set 'Users can create security groups in Azure portals, API or PowerShell' to No
Set 'Restrict access to Microsoft Entra admin center' to Yes
Set guest user access to the most restrictive level
Enable security defaults
questions.explain: These two user and group settings block non-admins while admins keep the rights through their roles. Restricting admin center access doesn't block Graph or PowerShell. Guest access settings affect guests only, and security defaults enforce MFA, not creation rights.

questions.stem: A cloud-only user was deleted by mistake. For how long can you restore the account from Deleted users?
options: 7 days
14 days
30 days
90 days
questions.explain: Deleted users remain soft-deleted for 30 days, during which they can be restored with their properties. After that they are permanently deleted.

questions.stem: For each statement about managing users, select Yes if true.

statements.s: To change the department of a user synced from on-premises AD, change it in AD rather than in Microsoft Entra ID.
Microsoft support can recover a user that was permanently deleted.
A restored user gets back the licences they had, even if no licences are currently available.

questions.explain: Synced attributes are mastered on-premises and the next sync would overwrite cloud edits. Permanently deleted users can't be recovered by anyone. Restoring brings back licences, which can temporarily push the tenant over its purchased count.

questions.stem: Complete the Microsoft Graph PowerShell command that creates a cloud user who must change the password at first sign-in.
options: PasswordProfile
PasswordPolicies
Password
InitialPassword
questions.explain: New-MgUser takes the password in the PasswordProfile parameter, a hashtable with Password and ForceChangePasswordNextSignIn. PasswordPolicies is a string such as DisablePasswordExpiration. Password and InitialPassword aren't New-MgUser parameters.

questions.stem: A project team needs a shared mailbox, a shared calendar and a SharePoint site created together. Which group type should you create?
options: Security group
Mail-enabled security group
Microsoft 365 group
Distribution list
questions.explain: Microsoft 365 groups provision a shared mailbox, calendar and SharePoint site. Security groups control access. Mail-enabled security groups and distribution lists deliver email but don't create a shared site or calendar.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra groups, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A Microsoft 365 group can contain device objects.
A group expiration policy applies to Microsoft 365 groups.
An owner can manually add a member to a dynamic membership group.

questions.explain: Microsoft 365 groups hold users only; devices need a security group. Expiration policies apply to Microsoft 365 groups. Dynamic group membership is controlled by the rule only, so manual additions aren't possible.

questions.stem: A dynamic group must include every user whose department is Sales or Marketing. Complete the membership rule.
options: -and
-or
-contains
-match
questions.explain: -or matches users who satisfy either expression. -and would require both departments at once (no user matches). -contains and -match are comparison operators used inside a single expression, not to join two expressions.

questions.stem: You need a dynamic group containing all internal users but no guest users. Which rule should you use?
options: user.objectId -ne null
(user.objectId -ne null) -and (user.userType -eq "Guest")
user.accountEnabled -eq true
(user.objectId -ne null) -and (user.userType -eq "Member")
questions.explain: Adding userType -eq "Member" removes guests. user.objectId -ne null alone includes guests, the Guest clause selects only guests, and accountEnabled includes enabled guests and excludes disabled members.

questions.case: Fabrikam has three dynamic user groups. Together they contain 1,500 memberships, but some users are in more than one group, so there are 1,200 unique users. Fabrikam also has a dynamic device group containing 300 Windows devices.
questions.stem: What is the minimum number of Microsoft Entra ID P1 licences Fabrikam needs for these dynamic groups?
questions.explain: P1 coverage is needed per unique user who is a member of any dynamic group, so 1,200. Overlapping memberships aren't counted twice, and device-based dynamic groups don't need licences.

questions.stem: A Global Administrator tries to create an attribute set for custom security attributes and is denied. Which role is the least-privileged role that can create attribute sets and attribute definitions?
options: Attribute Assignment Administrator
Attribute Definition Administrator
Directory Writers
Privileged Role Administrator
questions.explain: Attribute Definition Administrator manages attribute sets and definitions. Attribute Assignment Administrator only assigns values. Directory Writers and Privileged Role Administrator, like Global Administrator, don't get custom security attribute rights by default.

questions.stem: For each statement about custom security attributes, select Yes if true.

statements.s: By default, a Global Administrator can read custom security attribute values on users.
An attribute definition can be renamed after it is created.
'Only allow predefined values' can be changed from Yes to No.

questions.explain: Admin roles, including Global Administrator, can't read custom security attributes without an Attribute role. Attribute set and attribute names are fixed once created. Predefined-only can be relaxed from Yes to No, but not tightened from No to Yes.

questions.stem: You need to create 400 internal user accounts with the Bulk create feature. Put the steps in order.
options: Download the latest CSV template from Bulk create
Enter Name, User name and Initial password for each user, and remove the sample row
Upload the file and submit it after validation
Review status and errors on the Bulk operation results page
questions.explain: Start from the current template, fill in the required columns (displayName, userPrincipalName, passwordProfile), upload so the file is validated, then check Bulk operation results and download any error details.

questions.stem: You have a CSV of 200 partner contacts from other companies. Each needs a guest account and an email invitation. Which Entra admin center feature should you use?
options: Bulk invite
Bulk create
Download users
Bulk restore
questions.explain: Bulk invite creates guest (B2B) accounts and sends invitation emails. Bulk create makes internal member accounts without invitations, Download users exports a list, and Bulk restore recovers deleted users.

questions.stem: A script creates users from a CSV file using New-MgUser with delegated permissions. Complete the connection command with the least-privileged permission that allows creating users.
options: User.Read.All
Directory.Read.All
User.ReadWrite.All
Group.ReadWrite.All
questions.explain: Creating users needs write permission on users, so User.ReadWrite.All. The two Read scopes only allow reading, and Group.ReadWrite.All covers groups, not users.

questions.stem: Employees want to read work email on personal iPhones and Android phones that the company doesn't own. Which device identity fits?
options: Microsoft Entra joined
Microsoft Entra hybrid joined
Microsoft Entra registered
Windows Autopilot self-deploying
questions.explain: Personal (BYOD) and mobile devices are Microsoft Entra registered. Entra join is for organisation-owned Windows devices, hybrid join needs on-premises AD domain join, and Autopilot provisions corporate Windows devices.

questions.stem: You are configuring Microsoft Entra hybrid join for domain-joined Windows 11 devices in a managed (PHS) domain by using Microsoft Entra Connect. Which TWO actions are required? Select TWO.
options: Configure the service connection point (SCP) with Configure device options in Microsoft Entra Connect
Enrol every device in Microsoft Intune first
Make sure the OUs containing the computer objects are in the sync scope
Assign every user a Microsoft Entra ID P2 licence
Install the Microsoft Entra private network connector on each device
questions.explain: Hybrid join needs the SCP so devices find the tenant, and the computer objects must be synced. Intune enrolment is optional, hybrid join doesn't need P2, and the private network connector belongs to Application Proxy/Private Access.

questions.stem: You must require multifactor authentication whenever a user joins or registers a device with Microsoft Entra ID. What does Microsoft recommend?
options: Set 'Require multifactor authentication to register or join devices' to Yes
Turn on security defaults
Create an Intune enrolment restriction
Create a Conditional Access policy that targets the user action 'Register or join devices' and requires MFA
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends the Conditional Access user action Register or join devices with a grant control requiring MFA, leaving the legacy device setting at No. Security defaults are tenant-wide, and Intune restrictions control enrolment platforms, not MFA.

questions.stem: What is the default value of the 'Maximum number of devices per user' device setting?
options: Unlimited
questions.explain: The default is 50 Entra joined or registered devices per user, and it can be raised to 100. The limit doesn't apply to hybrid joined devices.

questions.stem: A new user is added to a group that has group-based licensing for Microsoft 365 E5. The licence shows the error 'Usage location isn't allowed'. What should you do?
options: Assign the licence directly to the user
Remove the Exchange Online service plan from the group assignment
Set the user's usage location, then reprocess the licence
Add the user to a nested group under the licensed group
questions.explain: This error means the usage location is missing or unsupported. Set it and reprocess. A direct assignment needs a usage location too, removing a service plan doesn't fix it, and nested group members don't inherit licences.

questions.case: Maya is moving from Sales to Finance. Each department's group has group-based licensing with different service plans enabled. Maya must not lose access to any service during the move.
questions.stem: Put the steps in order.
options: Add Maya to the Finance licensed group
Confirm on Maya's Licenses page that the Finance assignment applied without errors
Remove Maya from the Sales licensed group
questions.explain: Adding the new group first means Maya never has a gap. Check that the inherited licence applied correctly before removing her from the original group.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about group-based licensing are true? Select TWO.
options: Licences assigned to a parent group flow to members of nested groups
Only direct members of the licensed group receive the licence
A user can't hold the same product both directly and through a group
You can turn off individual service plans in a group licence assignment
Group-based licensing can't be used with dynamic groups
questions.explain: Nested groups aren't supported, so only direct members get licences, and service plans can be disabled per assignment. A user can have both a direct and an inherited assignment, and dynamic groups work with group-based licensing.

questions.stem: What is the default guest user access level in Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings?
options: Guest users have limited access to properties and memberships of directory objects
Guest users have the same access as members
Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects
Guest users have no access to the directory
questions.explain: Limited access is the default. Same access as members is the most inclusive option and 'restricted to their own objects' the most restrictive. There is no 'no access' option.

questions.stem: Guest invitations are limited to users in specific admin roles. A project manager who holds no admin role must be able to invite external partners. Which role is least privileged for this?
options: User Administrator
External Identity Provider Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator
Guest Inviter
questions.explain: Guest Inviter lets a user invite guests even when invites are limited to admin roles. User Administrator also works but grants far more. External Identity Provider Administrator manages IdPs, and Helpdesk Administrator resets passwords.

questions.stem: For each statement about external collaboration settings, select Yes if true.

statements.s: You can configure collaboration restrictions so that invitations are allowed only to domains you list.
Letting external users remove themselves from your organisation requires privacy information in the tenant properties.
Trusting MFA from a partner tenant is configured in external collaboration settings.

questions.explain: Collaboration restrictions support an allow list or a deny list. The leave setting is only available after a privacy contact and statement are added. MFA trust is an inbound trust setting in cross-tenant access settings.

questions.stem: Complete the Microsoft Graph PowerShell command that invites a partner and emails them an invitation that lands on My Apps.
options: New-MgUser
New-MgInvitation
New-MgUserInvitation
Add-MgGuestUser
questions.explain: New-MgInvitation calls the Graph invitations API and creates the guest. New-MgUser creates member accounts without invitations. New-MgUserInvitation and Add-MgGuestUser aren't Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets.

questions.stem: You invite jo@fabrikam.com to the contoso.onmicrosoft.com tenant. Before Jo redeems the invitation, what does the admin center show for the account?
options: UserType Member and status Accepted
UserType Guest and status Pending acceptance
UserType Guest and status Disabled
UserType Member and status Pending acceptance
questions.explain: Invited B2B users are created with UserType Guest, and until they redeem the status shows Pending acceptance. UserType Member is for internal or external members, and the account isn't disabled.

questions.stem: You are preparing the Bulk invite CSV in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Which TWO values are required for each row? Select TWO.
options: Email address to invite
Initial password
Redirection url
User principal name
Usage location
questions.explain: Bulk invite needs the invitee's email address and the redirection URL; the custom message is optional. Initial password and UPN are Bulk create columns, and guests aren't given a password by you. Usage location isn't required.

questions.stem: A guest's company was acquired and her email changed. She must keep all her group memberships and app assignments in your tenant but sign in with the new address. What should you do?
options: Delete the guest and invite the new address
Change her UserType to Member
Update her mail property, then reset her redemption status
Add the new address as an alternate UPN suffix
questions.explain: Reset redemption status lets her redeem with the new identity while keeping the object ID, groups and app assignments. Deleting loses those. UserType doesn't change sign-in identity, and UPN suffixes apply to your own domains.

questions.stem: For each statement about external user accounts, select Yes if true.

statements.s: UserType describes how the user signs in.
Helpdesk Administrator is the least-privileged role that can reset a guest's redemption status.
A user from another tenant can have UserType Member in your tenant.

questions.explain: UserType only describes the relationship to your organisation; the Identities property shows how the user signs in. Helpdesk Administrator is the least-privileged role for resetting redemption. External members, common in multitenant organisations, are external users with UserType Member.

questions.case: Contoso requires MFA for all users, including guests, through Conditional Access. Fabrikam guests already complete MFA in Fabrikam's own tenant and complain about being asked for MFA again by Contoso. Contoso must keep requiring MFA.
questions.stem: What should Contoso configure?
options: Exclude Fabrikam guests from the Conditional Access policy
Enable B2B direct connect outbound to Fabrikam
Disable email one-time passcode
In cross-tenant access settings, add Fabrikam and enable inbound trust of multifactor authentication from Microsoft Entra tenants
questions.explain: Inbound MFA trust lets Contoso's policy accept the MFA claim from Fabrikam, so MFA is still required but not repeated. Excluding guests removes the requirement. Direct connect outbound affects Contoso users going to Fabrikam, and OTP is unrelated.

questions.stem: Contoso and Fabrikam want users in each organisation to join each other's Teams shared channels without guest accounts. Which TWO configurations are required? Select TWO.
options: Contoso enables B2B direct connect inbound and outbound for Fabrikam in cross-tenant access settings
Fabrikam enables B2B direct connect inbound and outbound for Contoso in cross-tenant access settings
Contoso invites all Fabrikam users as guests
Both tenants configure cross-tenant synchronization
Both tenants add each other's domains to the collaboration restrictions allow list
questions.explain: B2B direct connect, used for Teams shared channels, is blocked by default and needs mutual configuration in both tenants. It doesn't create guest objects, so invitations and cross-tenant sync aren't needed; collaboration restrictions apply to B2B invitations.

questions.stem: For each statement about default cross-tenant access settings, select Yes if true.

statements.s: B2B collaboration is allowed inbound and outbound by default.
B2B direct connect is allowed by default.
MFA claims from other Microsoft Entra tenants are trusted by default.

questions.explain: By default, B2B collaboration is allowed both ways, B2B direct connect is blocked both ways, and MFA and device claims from other tenants aren't trusted until you configure inbound trust.

questions.case: Contoso (source) wants to synchronize its employees into Fabrikam (target) by using cross-tenant synchronization.
questions.stem: Put the steps in order.
options: In Fabrikam, allow user synchronization into this tenant and enable automatic redemption inbound for Contoso
In Contoso, enable automatic redemption outbound for Fabrikam
In Contoso, create a cross-tenant synchronization configuration and test the connection
In Contoso, assign users to the configuration and test with provision on demand
In Contoso, start provisioning and review the provisioning logs
questions.explain: The target must first allow inbound sync and auto-redemption, then the source enables outbound auto-redemption. The configuration is created and tested in the source, users are scoped and tested on demand, and then provisioning starts.

questions.stem: In which tenant do you create the cross-tenant synchronization configuration, and what user type does it create by default?
options: The target tenant; external guests
The source tenant; internal members
The target tenant; external members
The source tenant; external members
questions.explain: Cross-tenant synchronization is push-based and configured in the source tenant. By default it creates users as external members, which you can change to guests in the attribute mappings. Synced users are never internal members of the target.

questions.case: Contoso syncs users to Fabrikam with cross-tenant synchronization. An employee, Sam, leaves the project and is removed from the group assigned to the sync configuration in Contoso. Sam's account in Contoso stays enabled.
questions.stem: What happens to Sam's account in Fabrikam?
options: Nothing; it stays until a Fabrikam admin deletes it
It is soft-deleted in Fabrikam
It is converted to an external guest
It is immediately permanently deleted
questions.explain: When a user goes out of scope (unassigned, removed from an assigned group or no longer matching a filter), cross-tenant sync soft-deletes them in the target. It doesn't convert them to guests, and soft-deleted users are only hard-deleted after 30 days.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about a Microsoft Entra multitenant organization (MTO) are true? Select TWO.
options: It merges the member tenants into one directory with shared Conditional Access policies
It improves collaboration in new Microsoft Teams, such as notifications across the organisation's tenants
Users still have to be provisioned across tenants, typically with cross-tenant synchronization
It is configured only in the target tenant
It removes the need for cross-tenant access settings
questions.explain: An MTO is a tenant group that improves Teams and Viva Engage collaboration, and users are typically provisioned with cross-tenant sync. Tenants and their policies stay separate, an owner tenant creates it and others join, and each tenant pair is still governed by cross-tenant access settings.

questions.stem: Which identity provider can be used for self-service sign-up user flows but NOT for redeeming B2B invitations?
options: Facebook
Google
Microsoft account
Email one-time passcode
questions.explain: Facebook is supported only in self-service sign-up user flows. Google, Microsoft accounts and email one-time passcode can all be used to redeem invitations.

questions.case: Fabrikam uses a third-party SAML 2.0 identity provider. Contoso wants Fabrikam guests to sign in with their Fabrikam credentials. Fabrikam rotates its token-signing certificate every year, and Contoso wants no manual certificate updates.
questions.stem: Which THREE values should Contoso provide when creating the SAML/WS-Fed identity provider? Select THREE.
options: The partner IdP's issuer URI
The partner IdP's passive authentication endpoint
The partner IdP's metadata URL
Fabrikam's tenant ID in cross-tenant access settings
A client secret issued by the partner IdP
questions.explain: SAML/WS-Fed federation needs the issuer URI and passive authentication endpoint, and a metadata URL lets Microsoft Entra ID renew the signing certificate automatically. Tenant IDs apply to Entra-to-Entra cross-tenant settings, and client secrets apply to OAuth providers like Google.

questions.stem: You need a standby Microsoft Entra Connect Sync server that can quickly take over if the primary fails, without exporting changes while the primary is healthy. What should you deploy?
options: A second Entra Connect server in staging mode
A second active Entra Connect server for the same tenant
Three Microsoft Entra private network connectors
An Entra Connect Health agent on a second server
questions.explain: A staging-mode server imports and synchronises but doesn't export, so it's ready to become active. Two active servers for one tenant aren't supported. Private network connectors belong to Application Proxy, and Connect Health monitors but doesn't sync.

questions.stem: For each statement about installing Microsoft Entra Connect Sync, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Express settings need an on-premises Enterprise Admin account.
Entra Connect Sync can be installed on Windows Server Core.
The default SQL Server Express LocalDB supports about 100,000 objects.

questions.explain: Express settings need Enterprise Admin on-premises. Server Core isn't supported; a full GUI is required. LocalDB has a 10 GB limit, which is about 100,000 objects; larger directories need full SQL Server.

questions.stem: A new hire was just created in AD DS and must appear in Microsoft Entra ID now, without waiting for the next scheduled cycle. Complete the command on the sync server.
options: Initial
Full
Delta
Export
questions.explain: A Delta cycle imports and exports only changes, which is what's needed for a new object. Initial runs a slow full import and sync, used after configuration changes. Full and Export aren't valid PolicyType values.

questions.stem: You must change OU-based filtering on Microsoft Entra Connect Sync without a scheduled cycle running mid-change. Put the steps in order.
options: Run Set-ADSyncScheduler -SyncCycleEnabled $false
Change the OU selection in the Entra Connect wizard
Run Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Initial
Run Set-ADSyncScheduler -SyncCycleEnabled $true
questions.explain: Disable the scheduler first so no cycle runs with a half-finished configuration. Change filtering, then run an initial (full) cycle so the new scope is fully imported, and re-enable the scheduler.

questions.stem: What is the default synchronization interval of the Microsoft Entra Connect Sync scheduler?
options: 2 minutes
15 minutes
60 minutes
30 minutes
questions.explain: The scheduler runs a cycle every 30 minutes by default. Two minutes is the password hash sync and Cloud Sync interval. You can customise the interval with Set-ADSyncScheduler.

questions.case: Contoso acquired Litware. Litware's AD forest has no trust with Contoso's forests and won't get one. Contoso wants Litware users in its tenant quickly, with no single point of failure and minimal on-premises infrastructure. Litware users will use password hash sync.
questions.stem: What should Contoso deploy for Litware?
options: A second Entra Connect Sync server for the same tenant pointing at Litware
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync with three provisioning agents in Litware's forest
Cross-tenant synchronization from Litware's forest
Pass-through authentication agents in Litware's forest
questions.explain: Cloud Sync supports disconnected forests, uses lightweight agents and gives HA through multiple active agents. A second active Connect Sync server for one tenant isn't supported. Cross-tenant sync works between Entra tenants, not AD forests. PTA agents authenticate but don't sync.

questions.stem: Which TWO requirements mean you should choose Microsoft Entra Connect Sync rather than Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync? Select TWO.
options: Users must sign in with pass-through authentication
Attributes for one user must be merged from accounts in two different forests
Sync must continue automatically if one agent server fails
Password hash synchronization must be enabled
Users from a disconnected forest must be synced
questions.explain: PTA configuration and merging attributes across forests are Connect Sync features. Cloud Sync offers multiple active agents and disconnected-forest support, and both tools support PHS.

questions.stem: Contoso uses pass-through authentication and wants Microsoft Entra ID Protection to detect leaked credentials. What must Contoso also enable?
options: Seamless single sign-on
Password hash synchronization
Password writeback
Microsoft Entra Connect Health for AD DS
questions.explain: Leaked credentials detection compares hashes and needs password hash synchronization, which can run alongside PTA. Seamless SSO, password writeback and Connect Health don't supply password hashes.

questions.stem: For each statement about password hash synchronization, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Password changes sync about every 2 minutes, separately from the 30-minute object sync cycle.
The plaintext password is sent to Microsoft Entra ID over TLS.
By default, synced users' cloud passwords are set to never expire.

questions.explain: PHS runs roughly every 2 minutes. Only a salted PBKDF2 hash of the AD hash is sent; the plaintext is never known. By default Entra Connect sets DisablePasswordExpiration until you enable the cloud password policy feature for synced users.

questions.case: Woodgrove Bank's policy forbids storing any form of user password hash outside its datacentres. Logon hour restrictions in AD DS must apply to Microsoft 365 sign-ins immediately. The bank wants no inbound firewall rules and no federation servers.
questions.stem: Which sign-in method should Woodgrove use?
options: Password hash synchronization
AD FS federation
Pass-through authentication
Certificate-based authentication only
questions.explain: PTA validates passwords against AD DS through outbound-only agents, so no hash goes to the cloud and on-premises policies like logon hours apply. PHS stores a hash in the cloud, AD FS needs federation servers and inbound publishing, and CBA alone doesn't evaluate AD passwords.

questions.stem: Which network connectivity does a pass-through authentication agent need to Microsoft Entra ID?
options: Inbound TCP 443 from Microsoft Entra ID
Inbound TCP 88 (Kerberos) from Microsoft Entra ID
A site-to-site VPN to Azure
Outbound TCP 443 (and 80 for CRL checks)
questions.explain: PTA agents make outbound-only connections, using 443 for service traffic and 80 to download certificate revocation lists. No inbound ports, Kerberos from the cloud or VPN are needed.

questions.stem: You enable Seamless SSO with password hash synchronization. Which TWO statements are true? Select TWO.
options: A computer account named AZUREADSSOACC is created in AD DS
You should roll over the Kerberos decryption key at least every 30 days
Seamless SSO is required for SSO on Windows 11 Microsoft Entra joined devices
Seamless SSO requires AD FS
Each user needs a Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence
questions.explain: Enabling Seamless SSO creates AZUREADSSOACC, and Microsoft recommends rolling its key every 30 days. Entra joined Windows 10/11 devices use the PRT instead. Seamless SSO works with PHS or PTA, not AD FS, and it's free.

questions.stem: Seamless SSO is enabled, but users on domain-joined Windows 8.1 devices in the office are still prompted for a password in the browser. What should you check first?
options: That https://autologon.microsoftazuread-sso.com is in the browser's Local intranet zone
That the devices are Microsoft Entra registered
That staged rollout includes the users
That the users have Microsoft Authenticator registered
questions.explain: Browsers send Kerberos tickets only to sites in the Local intranet zone, so the autologon URL must be added (usually via Group Policy). Device registration, staged rollout and Authenticator don't control Kerberos ticket delivery.

questions.stem: You configured AD FS manually (not through Entra Connect). PHS is enabled and tested. Complete the command to switch contoso.com to cloud authentication.
options: "Federated"
"Managed"
"Cloud"
"PasswordHashSync"
questions.explain: A domain uses either Federated or Managed authentication; setting Managed switches it to cloud authentication (PHS or PTA). Cloud and PasswordHashSync aren't valid values, and Federated is the current state.

questions.case: Contoso wants to pilot password hash sync for 300 users while contoso.com stays federated with AD FS. The pilot users are in a dynamic group named PHS-Pilot.
questions.stem: For each statement about using staged rollout, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Contoso can add PHS-Pilot directly to staged rollout.
contoso.com stays federated while staged rollout is enabled.
Cloud-only users can be included in staged rollout.

questions.explain: Staged rollout supports security groups but not dynamic or nested groups, so Contoso needs an assigned group. The domain stays federated until you convert it. Only synced users are in scope; cloud-only users already use cloud authentication.

questions.stem: You plan to move apps from AD FS to Microsoft Entra ID and want a list of relying parties with their usage and migration readiness. What should you use, and what does it depend on?
options: The Sign-in logs, which depend on Microsoft Entra ID P2
The Provisioning logs, which depend on Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
The AD FS application activity report, which depends on Connect Health for AD FS agents
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps Cloud Discovery, which depends on firewall logs
questions.explain: The AD FS application activity report lists relying parties, usage and migration readiness from Connect Health for AD FS data. Sign-in and provisioning logs don't show AD FS relying parties, and Cloud Discovery finds SaaS usage from network logs.

questions.case: Contoso deploys Microsoft Entra Connect Health with one agent on the Entra Connect server, two agents on AD FS servers and one agent on a domain controller.
questions.stem: What is the minimum number of Microsoft Entra ID P1 licences Contoso needs for Connect Health?
questions.explain: The first agent needs 1 licence and each additional agent needs 25 more. Four agents need 1 + 25 x 3 = 76 licences. 4 assumes one licence per agent; 25 and 100 don't follow the 1 + 25-per-additional-agent rule.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra feature is now the single place to enable and scope authentication methods such as passkeys, Microsoft Authenticator and SMS for MFA and SSPR?
questions.explain: The Authentication methods policy (Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies) manages methods for both sign-in and SSPR. Management in the legacy MFA and SSPR policies ended on 30 September 2025, and Entra Connect only synchronises identities.
options: The Authentication methods policy
The legacy MFA service settings page
The SSPR Authentication methods blade
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync options

questions.stem: Your tenant has completed migration to the Authentication methods policy. For each statement, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: After Migration complete, legacy method settings are greyed out and ignored; the exception is SSPR security questions, which aren't yet in the Authentication methods policy.

statements.s: The migration state is Migration complete, and only the Authentication methods policy is used for MFA and SSPR methods.
Legacy MFA settings remain editable and override the Authentication methods policy.
Security questions for SSPR are still configured in the legacy SSPR settings.

questions.stem: A company with Microsoft Entra ID P1 wants to require MFA only for users outside the corporate network. Security defaults are currently enabled. What should the administrator do first?
questions.explain: Security defaults are on/off only and can't be customised or combined with custom Conditional Access policies; the admin must disable them and build a location-based policy. Per-user MFA is legacy and not location-aware.
options: Add the corporate network as an MFA trusted IP in security defaults
Disable security defaults so Conditional Access policies can be used
Customise security defaults to exclude the corporate network
Enable per-user MFA for remote users

questions.stem: After enabling Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication with default settings, what protection level do user certificates have?
questions.explain: The default authentication binding protection level is single-factor. To count as multifactor, add a rule by issuer or policy OID that maps certificates to multifactor.
options: Multifactor
Passwordless MFA
Single-factor
Phishing-resistant MFA

questions.stem: You're implementing Microsoft Entra CBA for smart card users. Put the steps in order.
questions.explain: Microsoft's order: trust store first so certificates can be validated, then enable CBA for a group, set authentication and username bindings, then test.
options: Upload the trusted CAs with CRL URLs to the PKI-based trust store
Enable certificate-based authentication for a target group in the Authentication methods policy
Configure the authentication binding (single-factor or multifactor rules)
Configure the username binding that maps a certificate field to a user attribute
Test sign-in and check the sign-in log for the binding used

questions.stem: A help desk operator with the Authentication Administrator role must issue a Temporary Access Pass to a Global Administrator who lost their security key. The operation fails. Which role is required?
questions.explain: Authentication Administrators can create TAPs only for non-admin users. Privileged Authentication Administrators can do it for admins. Authentication Policy Administrator configures the TAP policy but doesn't issue passes.
options: Authentication Policy Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator
Privileged Role Administrator
Privileged Authentication Administrator

questions.stem: Which statements about the Temporary Access Pass policy defaults are true? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Defaults: default lifetime 1 hour, maximum 8 hours (configurable up to 30 days), length 8, one-time use = false. A TAP doesn't replace the password; the password still works.
options: The maximum lifetime is 24 hours
Passes are one-time use by default
The default lifetime is 1 hour
The default passcode length is 8 characters
A TAP replaces the user's password while valid

questions.stem: Users are approving fraudulent MFA prompts. You want Authenticator notifications to show which app is being accessed and where the sign-in came from. What should you configure?
questions.explain: Additional context adds the app name and location to push and passwordless notifications. Number matching is already always on and can't be configured. Report suspicious activity lets users flag prompts but doesn't add context.
options: Additional context: show application name and geographic location
Number matching for push notifications
System-preferred multifactor authentication
Report suspicious activity

questions.stem: For each statement about passkeys (FIDO2) in Microsoft Entra ID, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: Synced passkeys can't be attested. Key restriction policies use AAGUIDs and apply at registration and sign-in. Registration requires MFA within the past five minutes.

statements.s: Synced passkeys stored in a cloud provider such as iCloud Keychain support attestation.
Key restrictions can allow or block specific authenticator models by AAGUID.
Users must have completed MFA within the last five minutes to register a passkey.

questions.case: Contoso issues every employee a hardware security key from one of two approved vendors. Auditors require proof that only these models can be registered.
questions.stem: Contoso must allow only two FIDO2 security key models it has purchased and must guarantee that the make and model are verified at registration. Which passkey profile configuration meets the goal?
questions.explain: An allow list of the two AAGUIDs restricts models; attestation must be enforced for Entra ID to verify make and model, otherwise AAGUID lists are only guidance. Blocking the AAGUIDs does the opposite.
options: Enforce attestation = No and key restrictions set to Allow with the two AAGUIDs
Enforce attestation = Yes and key restrictions set to Allow with the two AAGUIDs
Enforce attestation = No and key restrictions set to Block with the two AAGUIDs
Allow self-service set up = No and passkey type = Synced

questions.stem: A user receives an MFA prompt they didn't trigger and reports it using Report suspicious activity. What happens to the user in Microsoft Entra ID Protection?
questions.explain: Report suspicious activity sets the user to high user risk, so a risk-based Conditional Access policy can force remediation. It doesn't disable the account, and the legacy block/unblock list was retired.
options: The user's sign-in risk is set to medium
The user's account is automatically disabled
The user's risk is set to high
The user is added to the MFA blocked users list

questions.stem: Which legacy MFA features were replaced by Report suspicious activity? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Report suspicious activity replaced fraud alert, block/unblock users and the related email notifications, which were removed in March 2025. OATH tokens and trusted IPs are separate settings.
options: Block/unblock users
OATH tokens
Notifications
Trusted IPs
Fraud alert

questions.case: Northwind set Remember MFA on trusted devices to 30 days a long time ago. A new Conditional Access policy now requires a 12-hour sign-in frequency for the finance app, and the help desk is receiving complaints about prompts at odd times.
questions.stem: You are configuring a Conditional Access sign-in frequency of 12 hours for an app. Users report unpredictable MFA prompts. Which legacy setting should you disable first?
questions.explain: Microsoft advises disabling Remember MFA on trusted devices before configuring sign-in frequency because the two together cause unexpected prompts. The other features don't control reauthentication timing.
options: Report suspicious activity
Number matching
System-preferred multifactor authentication
Remember multifactor authentication on trusted devices

questions.stem: Hybrid users with password hash synchronization can reset passwords with SSPR, but the new passwords don't work on their domain-joined PCs. What should you enable?
questions.explain: Password writeback sends SSPR resets from Entra ID to on-premises AD DS. PTA validates passwords on-premises but doesn't write resets back, and Seamless SSO only provides silent sign-in.
options: Password writeback
Seamless single sign-on
Pass-through authentication
Microsoft Entra Password Protection DC agent

questions.stem: For each statement about SSPR for administrators, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: Admins use the two-gate policy, which prohibits security questions. Update-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy -AllowedToUseSspr:$false disables admin SSPR.

statements.s: In a tenant with a custom domain configured, administrator accounts are subject to a two-gate policy requiring two authentication methods.
Administrators can use security questions to reset their passwords.
Administrator SSPR can be turned off by setting AllowedToUseSspr to false on the authorization policy.

questions.stem: You want to pilot SSPR with one department before rolling it out to everyone. Which Self service password reset enabled option should you choose?
questions.explain: Selected lets you choose a single group for a controlled rollout. All has no exclusion option, and SSPR scope is set by group, not by administrative unit.
options: All, with the department as an exclusion
Selected, with the department's group
None, then assign the department a licence
Selected, with the department's administrative unit

questions.stem: Complete the Microsoft Graph PowerShell command to prevent administrators from using SSPR.
questions.explain: AllowedToUseSspr is a property of the tenant authorization policy, updated with Update-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy. The authentication methods policy controls methods, not admin SSPR eligibility.
options: Update-MgPolicyAuthenticationMethodPolicy
Update-MgDomain
Update-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy
Update-MgDirectorySetting

questions.stem: A hybrid organisation wants to deploy Windows Hello for Business with SSO to on-premises file shares and has no PKI. Which trust type should it use?
questions.explain: Cloud Kerberos trust uses Microsoft Entra Kerberos and needs no PKI; Microsoft recommends it for hybrid. Key trust requires DC certificates, and certificate trust requires PKI and AD FS.
options: Certificate trust
Hybrid AD FS trust
Key trust
Cloud Kerberos trust

questions.stem: You configure Windows Hello for Business cloud Kerberos trust with Intune. The Intune tenant-wide WHfB enrolment policy is not configured. Which settings must you enable in the settings catalog policy? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Both Use Windows Hello For Business and Use Cloud Trust For On Prem Auth are required. Require Security Device is optional but recommended. Use Certificate For On Prem Auth would switch to certificate trust.
options: Allow Passwordless Phone Sign-in
Use Certificate For On Prem Auth
Require Security Device
Use Cloud Trust For On Prem Auth
Use Windows Hello For Business

questions.stem: For each statement about Windows Hello for Business, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: The PIN only unlocks the private key on the device. WHfB counts as MFA. When both GPO and Intune apply, GPO wins and Intune settings are ignored.

statements.s: The user's PIN is sent to Microsoft Entra ID for verification at each sign-in.
Windows Hello for Business satisfies a Conditional Access Require multifactor authentication grant.
If both Group Policy and Intune configure WHfB on a device, Group Policy settings take precedence.

questions.stem: An employee was dismissed. You disabled their cloud-only account and selected Revoke sessions. They can still read files in a line-of-business web API for a short time. Why?
questions.explain: Revoking sessions invalidates refresh tokens; access tokens (about one hour) stay valid unless the resource supports continuous access evaluation. Revocation doesn't target only mobile devices.
options: Existing access tokens remain valid until they expire because the API isn't CAE-capable
Disabling an account takes 24 hours to replicate
Revoke sessions invalidates only access tokens, not refresh tokens
Revoke sessions only affects mobile devices

questions.stem: Complete the Microsoft Graph PowerShell script that disables a user and invalidates their refresh tokens.
questions.explain: Revoke-MgUserSignInSession revokes the user's Entra ID sign-in sessions and refresh tokens. Removing authentication methods doesn't end sessions, removing an OAuth2 permission grant only revokes delegated consent, and Remove-MgUser deletes the account.
options: Remove-MgUser
Revoke-MgUserSignInSession
Remove-MgOauth2PermissionGrant
Remove-MgUserAuthenticationMethod

questions.case: A Contoso engineer's synced account shows impossible travel and new inbox rules. Contoso uses Microsoft Entra Connect Sync with password hash synchronization. The security team needs to contain the account immediately.
questions.stem: A synced (hybrid) user's account is compromised. Put the containment steps in the order Microsoft recommends.
questions.explain: For hybrid users the source of authority is AD DS, so disable there first and reset the password twice to mitigate pass-the-hash, then revoke cloud sessions and disable devices.
options: Disable the account in on-premises Active Directory
Reset the user's AD password twice
Revoke the user's Microsoft Entra sessions
Disable the user's registered devices

questions.stem: You deployed the Microsoft Entra Password Protection proxy and DC agents. You want to log which passwords would be rejected without affecting users. Which mode should you select?
questions.explain: Audit mode logs weak passwords in the event log but still accepts them. Enforced rejects them. Report-only is a Conditional Access state, not a Password Protection mode.
options: Disabled
Enforced
Audit
Report-only

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra Password Protection and smart lockout, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: The custom list holds up to 1,000 terms, and passwords need at least 5 points. Customising smart lockout requires Entra ID P1 or higher; the defaults (10 attempts, 60 seconds) are always on.

statements.s: The custom banned password list can contain up to 1,000 terms.
A password must score at least 5 points after banned terms are counted to be accepted.
Smart lockout's lockout threshold and duration can be customised with Microsoft Entra ID Free.

questions.case: Fabrikam uses Microsoft Entra Connect with pass-through authentication. Its domain account lockout policy is 10 invalid attempts with a 1-minute lockout duration. Password spray attempts through Entra ID are locking employees out of on-premises resources.
questions.stem: You use pass-through authentication. On-premises AD DS locks accounts after 10 bad attempts for 1 minute. Attackers are locking users out of AD. How should you configure smart lockout?
questions.explain: With PTA, the Entra smart lockout threshold must be lower than AD DS (AD should be 2-3x higher) and the Entra duration longer, so Entra blocks attackers before AD locks the account. Smart lockout can't be disabled.
options: Set the Entra threshold higher than 10 and the duration shorter than 60 seconds
Set the Entra threshold equal to 10 and the duration equal to 60 seconds
Disable smart lockout and rely on AD DS lockout
Set the Entra threshold lower than 10 and the lockout duration longer than 60 seconds

questions.stem: Complete the command that creates the Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object for a domain.
questions.explain: Set-AzureADKerberosServer creates (and with -RotateServerKey rotates) the Kerberos server object and publishes it to Entra ID. Get- only views it, Remove- deletes it, and Set-ADComputer edits ordinary AD computer objects.
options: Set-AzureADKerberosServer
Remove-AzureADKerberosServer
Get-AzureADKerberosServer
Set-ADComputer

questions.stem: Which statements about Microsoft Entra Kerberos are true? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Entra ID issues a partial TGT (SID, no groups) that DCs exchange for a full TGT. The server object is an RODC-like computer object plus krbtgt_AzureAD, not a real DC. Setup needs Domain/Enterprise Admins and Hybrid Identity Administrator.
options: Entra ID issues a partial TGT that an on-premises DC exchanges for a full TGT
Running Set-AzureADKerberosServer requires only the Global Reader role
Entra ID issues a full TGT with all group memberships directly to the client
The Kerberos server object includes a disabled krbtgt_AzureAD user account
The Kerberos server object is a full writable domain controller in Azure

questions.stem: For each statement about how multiple Conditional Access policies interact, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: All applicable policies apply together: every grant requirement must be met and Block always wins. Conditional Access has no policy priority order.

statements.s: If two policies apply and one requires MFA while the other requires a compliant device, the user must satisfy both.
Policies are processed in priority order and evaluation stops at the first matching policy.
If any applicable policy blocks access, access is blocked even if another policy grants it.

questions.stem: You're designing your first Conditional Access policies. Which accounts does Microsoft recommend excluding from every policy?
questions.explain: Excluding break-glass accounts prevents a misconfigured policy from locking everyone out. Excluding all admins or guests would leave high-value or external accounts unprotected.
options: Accounts with the Conditional Access Administrator role
Emergency access (break-glass) accounts
Guest users
All Global Administrators

questions.stem: Which licences or prerequisites are needed for a Conditional Access policy that uses the sign-in risk condition? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Risk conditions come from ID Protection, which needs P2 or Entra Suite, and custom Conditional Access requires security defaults to be off. Workload Identities Premium is for service principal risk; Intune and Defender for Cloud Apps aren't required.
options: Microsoft Entra ID P2 (or Microsoft Entra Suite)
Microsoft Intune Plan 1
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Workload Identities Premium
Security defaults disabled

questions.stem: You need a Conditional Access policy that blocks legacy authentication protocols such as IMAP and POP3. Which client apps should you select?
questions.explain: Legacy authentication is represented by Exchange ActiveSync clients and Other clients (SMTP, IMAP, POP3, MAPI and similar). Browser and Mobile apps and desktop clients are modern authentication.
options: Browser only
Mobile apps and desktop clients only
Exchange ActiveSync clients and Other clients
Browser and Mobile apps and desktop clients

questions.stem: You must require MFA for anyone managing Azure resources through the Azure portal, Azure PowerShell or Azure CLI. Which target resource should the policy use?
questions.explain: Windows Azure Service Management API covers ARM, the Azure portal, Azure PowerShell and Azure CLI. Microsoft Admin Portals covers admin portals but not CLI/PowerShell access to ARM, and Office 365 covers productivity workloads.
options: Microsoft Admin Portals
Office 365
Microsoft Graph PowerShell
Windows Azure Service Management API

questions.stem: For each statement about named locations, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: Only IP-based named locations can be trusted. Ranges must be public egress IPs, not private client addresses. All trusted networks and locations includes trusted IP locations and legacy MFA trusted IPs.

statements.s: Country/region named locations can be marked as trusted.
IP ranges in named locations should be the public egress addresses of the network.
Selecting All trusted networks and locations also includes MFA trusted IPs if configured.

questions.case: Litware's admins use dedicated privileged access workstations (PAWs). Intune sets extensionAttribute1 to 'PAW' on these devices. Security wants admin access to Azure blocked from any other device.
questions.stem: You need a Conditional Access policy that blocks access to the Azure portal from every device except privileged access workstations, which have extensionAttribute1 set to 'PAW'. Which condition should you use?
questions.explain: Filter for devices lets you include or exclude devices by properties such as extensionAttribute1. Platforms can't distinguish PAWs from other Windows PCs, and named locations require public IPs, not device identity.
options: Filter for devices with a rule on device.extensionAttribute1
Client apps set to Browser
A named location containing the workstations' private IP addresses
Device platforms with Windows excluded

questions.stem: Complete the Conditional Access policy JSON (Microsoft Graph) so that the policy applies to legacy authentication clients.
questions.explain: Legacy authentication maps to the client app types exchangeActiveSync and other. browser and mobileAppsAndDesktopClients are modern authentication; platforms and risk levels don't identify legacy protocols.
options: "signInRiskLevels": ["high"]
"clientAppTypes": ["exchangeActiveSync", "other"]
"platforms": { "includePlatforms": ["all"] }
"clientAppTypes": ["browser", "mobileAppsAndDesktopClients"]

questions.stem: Administrators must sign in with a FIDO2 security key, Windows Hello for Business or multifactor certificate-based authentication. Which grant control should the policy use?
questions.explain: The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength allows FIDO2, WHfB/platform credential and multifactor CBA. Require MFA also accepts SMS or push, and Passwordless MFA additionally allows Authenticator phone sign-in.
options: Require multifactor authentication
Require authentication strength: Passwordless MFA
Require authentication strength: Phishing-resistant MFA
Require device to be marked as compliant

questions.stem: A policy must allow access from either Intune-compliant devices or domain-joined Windows devices synced to Entra ID. How should you configure the grant controls?
questions.explain: Require one of the selected controls is OR logic, so either device state satisfies it. Require all (AND) would need both at once. App protection policy relates to mobile apps, not domain-joined PCs.
options: Select only Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
Select compliant device and hybrid joined device with Require all the selected controls
Select Require app protection policy with Require one of the selected controls
Select compliant device and hybrid joined device with Require one of the selected controls

questions.stem: Complete the Microsoft Graph grantControls block so users must satisfy MFA AND have a compliant device.
questions.explain: The operator property controls combination: AND means all listed controls are required, OR means one is enough. requireAll and mode aren't properties of grantControls.
options: "operator": "AND"
"requireAll": true
"operator": "OR"
"mode": "block"

questions.case: Adatum allows staff to read email on personal phones. Staff refuse to enrol their phones in Intune, but compliance requires that corporate mail can't be copied into personal apps.
questions.stem: Employees use personal iOS and Android phones that aren't enrolled in Intune. Outlook mobile must protect corporate data in the app. Which grant control should you use for new policies?
questions.explain: App protection policy (Intune MAM) works without device enrolment. Compliant device requires enrolment; Require approved client app is retiring and new policies should use app protection policy; hybrid join applies to Windows.
options: Require device to be marked as compliant
Require app protection policy
Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device
Require approved client app

questions.stem: A Conditional Access policy is in report-only mode. A user signs in and would have been prompted for MFA. What result appears in the sign-in log's Report-only tab?
questions.explain: User action required means the conditions matched and an interactive control such as MFA would have been required. Failure is for non-interactive controls like block; Success means already satisfied; Not applied means conditions didn't match.
options: Report-only: Success
Report-only: Not applied
Report-only: User action required
Report-only: Failure

questions.stem: You use the What If tool to test a new policy, but the policy doesn't appear in the results. The policy state is Off. What should you do?
questions.explain: What If evaluates only enabled and report-only policies. Switching to report-only lets you simulate it safely. Roles and replication delays don't explain an Off policy being ignored.
options: Add the test user to the policy's exclusions
Assign the Security Reader role to the test user
Wait 24 hours for the policy to replicate
Set the policy to Report-only and run What If again

questions.stem: You want to use the Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook. Which prerequisites are required? Select TWO.
questions.explain: The workbook needs Entra ID P1 and sign-in logs streamed to a Log Analytics workspace. Microsoft Sentinel, ID Governance and Key Vault aren't required.
options: Microsoft Sentinel
A Log Analytics workspace receiving Entra sign-in logs
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
An Azure Key Vault
Microsoft Entra ID P1

questions.stem: Complete the KQL query to list sign-ins that Conditional Access blocked or that failed a Conditional Access requirement in the last day.
questions.explain: ConditionalAccessStatus holds success, failure or notApplied for enforced policies. ResultType is an error code, report-only outcomes live inside ConditionalAccessPolicies, and RiskState relates to ID Protection.
options: ConditionalAccessStatus == "failure"
ResultType == "notApplied"
ConditionalAccessStatus == "reportOnlyFailure"
RiskState == "atRisk"
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ____
| project UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, ConditionalAccessPolicies

questions.stem: Users of unmanaged devices must reauthenticate every 4 hours when using Microsoft 365. Which session control should you configure?
questions.explain: Sign-in frequency defines how often users must reauthenticate. Persistent browser session only controls whether the browser keeps the session after closing; CAE and app enforced restrictions don't set reauthentication intervals.
options: Persistent browser session set to Never persistent
Sign-in frequency set to 4 hours
Customize continuous access evaluation
Use app enforced restrictions

questions.stem: For each statement about Conditional Access session controls, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: The default is a rolling 90 days. Every time allows five minutes of clock skew. Persistent browser session requires the policy to target All resources.

statements.s: The default Microsoft Entra session behaviour is a rolling 90-day window.
Sign-in frequency set to Every time prompts users at most once every five minutes because of clock skew tolerance.
The persistent browser session control can be scoped to a single app rather than All resources.

questions.stem: Complete the Microsoft Graph sessionControls block to require reauthentication every 8 hours.
questions.explain: signInFrequency uses value plus type (hours or days) and isEnabled. everyTime is expressed through frequencyInterval, not type; unit and interval aren't valid properties.
options: "type": "everyTime"
"unit": "minutes"
"type": "hours"
"interval": "daily"

questions.case: After a token-theft incident, Fabrikam's security team wants stolen tokens replayed from an attacker's machine to be rejected for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Teams on managed Windows devices.
questions.stem: A tenant wants sign-in session tokens to be accepted only from the device they were issued to, reducing token replay for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Teams desktop apps on Windows. Which session control should be used?
questions.explain: Token protection ensures only device-bound sign-in session tokens are accepted, stopping replay from another device. Resilience defaults affect outages; App Control proxies sessions through Defender for Cloud Apps; Every time doesn't bind tokens.
options: Disable resilience defaults
Sign-in frequency: Every time
Use Conditional Access App Control
Require token protection for sign-in sessions

questions.stem: Contractors on unmanaged laptops must be able to view SharePoint Online in a browser but not download, print or sync files. What should you configure?
questions.explain: App enforced restrictions pass device state to SharePoint, which gives unmanaged devices browser-only limited access. Requiring a compliant device would block contractors entirely; app protection policy targets mobile apps.
options: The Use app enforced restrictions session control with SharePoint limited access
Require device to be marked as compliant
Require app protection policy
Persistent browser session set to Never persistent

questions.stem: Which statements about the Require device to be marked as compliant grant control are true? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Intune or a supported MDM sets compliance; InPrivate doesn't send device identity so it fails. Registration alone isn't compliance, and the control supports Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and Linux Ubuntu without requiring hybrid join.
options: Microsoft Edge InPrivate sessions are treated as non-compliant
It requires the device to be hybrid joined
It applies only to Windows devices
It is satisfied by any device registered in Microsoft Entra ID
Compliance is evaluated by Microsoft Intune or a supported partner MDM

questions.stem: You must block Microsoft 365 access from operating systems you don't support, such as ChromeOS, while allowing Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. How should you configure the device platforms condition?
