questions.explain: Access package assignment managers assign and remove users and manage requests, but can't create or edit packages. Access package managers can edit packages and policies, catalog owners control the whole catalog, and catalog readers can only view.

questions.stem: Which resources can you add to an entitlement management catalog? Select THREE.
options: Exchange Online distribution group
SharePoint Online site
Group synchronized from on-premises AD DS
Enterprise application integrated with Microsoft Entra ID
Cloud-created security group
questions.explain: Catalogs accept cloud-created security and Microsoft 365 groups, enterprise applications and SharePoint Online sites. Groups synchronized from on-premises AD DS and Exchange Online distribution groups can't be added.

questions.case: Contoso created a Partners catalog with Enabled for external users set to No. An access package in it has a policy For users not in your directory scoped to All configured connected organizations. Fabrikam is a configured connected organization, but Fabrikam users can't request the package.
questions.stem: What should you change so that partner users can request the package?
options: Set Hidden to No on the access package
Turn off Block external user from signing in in the external user lifecycle settings
Assign the partner sponsors the Catalog reader role
Set Enabled for external users to Yes on the Partners catalog
questions.explain: Connected-organization users can request a catalog's packages only when the catalog's Enabled for external users setting is Yes. Hidden only affects browsing in My Access. Lifecycle blocking applies after the last assignment ends, and Catalog reader gives view rights only.

questions.stem: You create a catalog with Microsoft Graph PowerShell. Complete the command.
options: New-MgEntitlementManagementCatalog
New-MgEntitlementManagementAccessPackage
New-MgIdentityGovernanceAccessReviewDefinition
New-MgGroup
questions.explain: New-MgEntitlementManagementCatalog creates a catalog in the Microsoft.Graph.Identity.Governance module. The access package cmdlet creates a package inside a catalog, the access review cmdlet creates review definitions, and New-MgGroup creates a group.

questions.stem: Which access package policy option prevents anyone from requesting the package so that only administrators or managers assign it?
options: For users in your directory, with Hidden set to Yes
None (administrator direct assignments only)
For users not in your directory
For users in your directory, with Require approval set to Yes
questions.explain: The None (administrator direct assignments only) option allows no requests; managers assign users directly and lifecycle settings still apply. Hidden packages can still be requested by link, and the other options allow requests.

questions.stem: You set Hidden to Yes on an access package. What is the effect?
options: No user can request the package until Hidden is set to No
Only administrators can see existing assignments
In-scope users don't see it when browsing My Access but can still request it with the direct link
All existing assignments are suspended
questions.explain: Hidden only removes the package from browsing in My Access. Users the policy allows can still request it through its direct link. Hidden doesn't block requests or change existing assignments.

questions.stem: You configure the approval settings of an access package policy. Which configurations are supported? Select TWO.
options: Five sequential approval stages
Up to three approval stages, each with its own approvers
Every listed approver in a stage must approve
Sponsors of the connected organization as approvers
questions.explain: Policies support one to three approval stages, and only one approver per stage needs to decide. Approvers can be managers, internal or external sponsors, or specific users. Five stages isn't supported.

questions.stem: You create a new access package in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Put the steps in order.
options: On Basics, enter a name and select the catalog
Add resource roles such as group membership or app roles
Configure the request policy: who can request and the approvals
Set lifecycle options such as expiration and access reviews
Review and create the access package
questions.explain: The wizard runs Basics (name, catalog), Resource roles, Requests (policy scope and approval), Requestor information and Lifecycle, then Review + create.

questions.case: Contoso has two access packages, Development environment and Production environment. Users holding one of them must never be able to request or be assigned the other, whichever they got first. Existing overlaps will be handled separately.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: On the Production package only, add the Development package as an incompatible access package
Create a monthly access review of both packages' assignments
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks users holding both packages
On each access package, add the other package as an incompatible access package
questions.explain: Separation of duties rules are one-directional, so you must configure the rule on both packages to block both directions. Access reviews find overlap only after it exists, and Conditional Access can't evaluate access package assignments.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Adding an incompatible access package removes existing assignments of users who hold both packages.
An access package assignment can be set to expire after a number of hours.
A policy can allow users to request an extension before their assignment expires.

questions.explain: Separation of duties only blocks new requests and assignments; existing overlaps stay and appear under Additional access. Lifecycle expiry can be a date, days, hours or never, and Allow users to extend access lets users request more time.

questions.stem: When a request for an access package is approved, a Logic App must create a ticket in the company's ITSM tool. What should you configure?
options: A custom extension in the catalog, linked to the access package policy
An automatic assignment policy
A lifecycle workflow with a joiner template
A terms of use requirement on the policy
questions.explain: Custom extensions call Azure Logic Apps at entitlement management stages such as request approved or assignment granted. Automatic assignment policies assign by attribute, lifecycle workflows run joiner/mover/leaver tasks, and terms of use don't call external systems.

questions.stem: Which portal do users use to request access packages and to approve requests?
options: My Apps (myapps.microsoft.com)
My Access (myaccess.microsoft.com)
My Account (myaccount.microsoft.com)
My Groups (mygroups.microsoft.com)
questions.explain: My Access is the portal for access package requests, approvals and access reviews. My Apps launches applications, My Account manages the user's profile and security info, and My Groups manages group membership.

questions.stem: A request shows Partially delivered because provisioning to one SharePoint site failed. After you fix the cause, what should the access package manager do?
options: Remove the request and ask the user to re-request
Recreate the access package
Reprocess the request
Start an access review of the package
questions.explain: Requests in Partially delivered or failed states can be reprocessed to retry delivery without a new request. Removing the request only deletes the record, recreating the package is unnecessary, and an access review doesn't deliver access.

questions.stem: You select Remove on a Delivered request on an access package's Requests page. What happens to the user's access?
options: The assignment and all resource access are removed immediately
The assignment is set to expire in 30 days
The user is blocked from signing in
The access remains; only the request record is deleted
questions.explain: Removing a completed request deletes only the request record. To revoke access, remove the user's assignment on the Assignments page.

questions.stem: A user's pending access package request changes to the Expired state. What does this mean?
options: No approver decided before the request timed out, so the user must submit a new request
The request was approved but provisioning to a resource failed
A second-stage approver denied the request
The user canceled the request in My Access
questions.explain: Expired means the approval deadline passed without a decision. A failed resource gives Partially delivered or failed, a denial gives Denied, and cancellation is separate.

questions.stem: How is a Microsoft Entra terms of use policy enforced?
options: As an Intune device compliance policy
As a grant control in a Conditional Access policy
As a Conditional Access session control
As an app consent policy
questions.explain: Terms of use appear as a grant control in Conditional Access: the user must accept the terms before access is granted. They aren't a session control, compliance policy or consent policy.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: You can edit the PDF of an existing terms of use in place without uploading a new version.
Require users to consent on every device is supported for B2B guest users.
Terms of use requires at least Microsoft Entra ID P1.

questions.explain: An uploaded document can't be changed; you upload a new version and can require re-acceptance. Per-device consent needs Entra-registered devices and isn't supported for B2B guests. Terms of use needs Entra ID P1 or higher.

questions.stem: You upload a new version of a terms of use PDF. All users must accept the new version the next time they access a covered resource. What should you select?
options: Expire consents
Require users to expand the terms of use
Require reaccept
Duration before re-acceptance required (days)
questions.explain: Require reaccept forces acceptance of the new version at next access. Expire consents and the re-acceptance duration set recurring schedules, and Require users to expand only makes users open the document before accepting.

questions.stem: An external user with no account in your tenant gets access through an access package. Default lifecycle settings apply. Put the events in order.
options: The user requests the package in My Access
The request is approved and the user is added as a B2B guest
The user's last access package assignment expires
The guest is blocked from signing in
The guest account is removed after 30 days
questions.explain: Entitlement management invites the approved external user as a guest. When the last assignment ends, the defaults block sign-in and then remove the guest after 30 days.

questions.case: Ben, a partner, was invited manually as a guest last year. This year he got the Project X access package, his only package. External user lifecycle settings are set to block sign-in and remove after 30 days. His assignment expired 45 days ago. Nobody marked him as governed.
questions.stem: What happens to Ben's guest account?
options: It's removed 30 days after the assignment expired
It's blocked from signing in and removed immediately
It's converted to a member account
It remains, because Ben wasn't invited through entitlement management
questions.explain: Lifecycle actions apply only to guests that entitlement management invited, or that were marked as governed. Ben was invited manually before the package, so his account stays.

questions.case: An access package policy that targeted All users let Litware staff request access, and a connected organization for Litware was created automatically. A new package policy targets All configured connected organizations, but Litware users can't request it.
questions.stem: What should you do so that the policy covers Litware users?
options: Change Litware's connected organization state to Configured
Add litware.com to the B2B collaboration allow list
Enable email one-time passcode authentication
Add an external sponsor from Litware
questions.explain: Proposed connected organizations, which are created automatically, aren't included in All configured connected organizations policies. Changing the state to Configured brings them in scope. Allow lists, one-time passcode and sponsors don't change the state.

questions.stem: Who can be an external sponsor of a connected organization?
options: A member user of your directory
A guest user from that organization who is already in your directory
Any email address in the partner's domain, even if not invited
Any user with the Connected Organization Administrator role
questions.explain: External sponsors are guests from the connected organization already in your directory. Internal sponsors are your member users. Sponsors must exist in your directory, and the Connected Organization Administrator role manages connected organizations but doesn't make anyone a sponsor.

questions.stem: Where do you create an access review of Microsoft Entra role assignments such as Global Administrator?
options: In Access reviews, by choosing Teams + Groups
In Entitlement management, on a catalog
In Privileged Identity Management, under Microsoft Entra roles > Access reviews
In Conditional Access, under Terms of use
questions.explain: Reviews of Entra roles and Azure resource roles are created from PIM. The group/app wizard covers Teams, groups and applications, entitlement management covers access package assignments, and terms of use isn't a review feature.

questions.stem: Group owners must create access reviews for the groups they own. They currently can't. What should you change?
options: Assign each owner the Catalog owner role
Make the owners reviewers in an existing review
Enable self-service group management in Groups settings
Set Group owners can create and manage access reviews for groups they own to Yes
questions.explain: That access reviews setting defaults to No. Turning it on lets group owners create and manage reviews for their groups. Catalog owner is an entitlement management role, being a reviewer doesn't allow creating reviews, and self-service group management is unrelated.

questions.stem: Your tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P2 licences. You plan a review scoped only to inactive users that also shows user-to-group affiliation recommendations. What do you need?
options: Microsoft Entra ID Governance licences
Microsoft Entra ID P1 licences
Microsoft 365 E3 licences
No more licences; Entra ID P2 includes these
questions.explain: Reviews scoped only to inactive users, and machine-learning recommendations such as user-to-group affiliation, need Microsoft Entra ID Governance. P2 covers basic access review features.

questions.stem: Which reviewer options can you select when creating an access review of a Microsoft 365 group? Select THREE.
options: Managers of users
Every Global Reader automatically
Group owner(s)
Users review their own access
The Directory Synchronization Accounts role
questions.explain: Group reviews support group owners, selected users or groups, self-review and managers, with fallback reviewers. Reviewer roles aren't assigned automatically to Global Readers or sync accounts.

questions.stem: In the Upon completion settings, you want the system recommendation, based on sign-in activity, to decide for users the reviewers didn't review. Which option should you select for If reviewers don't respond?
options: No change
Take recommendations
Remove access
Approve access
questions.explain: Take recommendations applies the decision helper result, such as no sign-in in 30 days, to unreviewed users. No change and Approve access keep access, and Remove access removes it whatever the activity.

questions.case: Fabrikam reviews guests in all Microsoft 365 groups quarterly. Denied guests must lose all access to the tenant, but admins need a grace period to reverse mistakes before the guest object is deleted.
questions.stem: Which setting should you use?
options: Denied guests: Remove user's membership from the resource
If reviewers don't respond: Remove access
Denied guests: Block user from signing in for 30 days, then remove user from the tenant
If reviewers don't respond: Take recommendations
questions.explain: Only the block-then-remove option removes denied guests from the tenant, with a 30-day window when admins can restore access. Removing membership leaves the guest account, and the reviewers-don't-respond options control unreviewed users, not denied ones.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A review that recurs weekly can have a duration of 14 days.
By default, reviewers get a reminder at the midpoint of the review.
Users added to a group after a review instance starts are reviewed in the next instance.

questions.explain: The duration must fit inside the recurrence interval, so weekly allows up to 7 days. Reminders go out halfway through. Each instance takes a snapshot at start, so later changes appear in the next cycle.

questions.stem: You create an access review of a group in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Put the steps in order.
options: Select Teams + Groups and choose the group and user scope
Choose the reviewers
Set the duration and recurrence
Configure the upon completion settings
Review and create the review
questions.explain: The wizard asks what to review and the scope, then reviewers, then schedule (duration, recurrence), then settings such as auto-apply and decision helpers, and finally Review + Create.

questions.stem: You automate access review creation with Microsoft Graph PowerShell. $params holds the review settings. Complete the command.
options: Get-MgIdentityGovernanceAccessReviewDefinition
New-MgEntitlementManagementAssignmentPolicy
New-MgEntitlementManagementAccessPackage
New-MgIdentityGovernanceAccessReviewDefinition
questions.explain: Access reviews are created as definitions (POST /identityGovernance/accessReviews/definitions), which is New-MgIdentityGovernanceAccessReviewDefinition. Get- only reads definitions, and the entitlement management cmdlets create policies and packages.

questions.stem: Auditors want one CSV of all application access review decisions from the past 12 months, filtered to Deny results. What should you use?
options: A Review History report under Access reviews
Download on each review instance's Results page
The Usage & insights report
The Sign-ins using legacy authentication workbook
questions.explain: Review History builds one CSV across many reviews, filtered by date range, review type and result. Download on Results exports a single instance, and the other reports don't contain review decisions.

questions.stem: After you create a Review History report, how long is it available to download?
options: 7 days
30 days
90 days
365 days
questions.explain: Review history reports stay downloadable for 30 days after they're created. For longer retention, keep the CSVs or route audit logs to Log Analytics or storage.

questions.stem: A reviewer is unsure whether a user still needs access. The reviewer wants the user to keep access for now and the uncertainty recorded. Which decision should the reviewer choose?
options: Approve, without a reason
Accept recommendations
Don't know
Deny
questions.explain: Don't know keeps the user's access and records the choice in the audit logs for others to see. Approve records a firm decision, Accept recommendations applies system advice that might deny, and Deny removes access.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A stopped access review instance can be restarted.
A denied user is removed as soon as the reviewer submits the decision.
If Auto apply results is off, an administrator can apply results from the instance in Review history.

questions.explain: Stopped reviews can't be restarted. Denials take effect only after the review ends or is stopped, and only if results are applied. With auto-apply off, an admin opens the instance and selects Apply.

questions.case: An access review of the group Sales-Sync, which Microsoft Entra Connect synchronizes from AD DS, ended with Auto apply results enabled. Reviewers denied 15 users, but all 15 are still members.
questions.stem: Why weren't the denied users removed?
options: The reviewers weren't the group owners
Justification wasn't required for the decisions
The review must also be reset before results apply
Review results can't change membership of groups synchronized from on-premises AD DS
questions.explain: Applying results doesn't change on-premises synced groups; the change must be made in AD DS. Reviewer type, justification and reset don't stop results being applied to cloud groups.

questions.stem: In PIM, which assignment type requires the user to take an action, such as completing MFA, before using the role?
options: Eligible
Active
Permanent active
Time-bound active
questions.explain: Eligible assignments must be activated before use, and activation can require MFA, justification or approval. Active assignments, permanent or time-bound, always apply with no activation.

questions.stem: A contractor must be able to use User Administrator just-in-time for the next three months only. What assignment should you create in PIM?
options: Active, permanent
Eligible, time-bound, ending in three months
Eligible, permanent
Active, time-bound, ending in three months
questions.explain: Just-in-time use needs an eligible assignment, and the three-month limit needs a time-bound end date. Active assignments give standing access, and a permanent eligible assignment never expires.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A PIM role assignment can last as little as one minute.
Some Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned in PIM with an administrative unit scope.
PIM automatically removes the last Global Administrator assignment when it expires.

questions.explain: Assignments must last at least five minutes. Supported roles can be scoped to an administrative unit or an application. PIM won't automatically remove the last Global Administrator assignment, to avoid lockout.

questions.stem: You use Microsoft Graph to give a user a permanent eligible assignment to Global Reader. Complete the request body.
options: selfActivate
adminRemove
adminAssign
selfExtend
questions.explain: An administrator creating an assignment uses adminAssign. selfActivate is what an eligible user sends to activate a role, adminRemove deletes an assignment, and selfExtend asks to extend an expiring assignment.

questions.stem: What range can you set for Activation maximum duration in PIM role settings?
options: 1 to 8 hours
30 minutes to 72 hours
1 to 7 days
1 to 24 hours
questions.explain: The Activation maximum duration slider runs from 1 to 24 hours, for both Microsoft Entra roles and Azure resource roles.

questions.stem: A Microsoft Entra role's PIM settings require approval to activate, but no approvers are selected. Who approves activation requests?
options: Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators
The requester's manager
Security Administrators
Nobody; the request can't be submitted
questions.explain: For Entra roles, if no approvers are specified, active Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators are the default approvers. Microsoft recommends naming specific approvers so you can't get locked out.

questions.case: Contoso's Global Administrators activate their eligible role in PIM. Security requires that every activation is done with a phishing-resistant method such as a FIDO2 passkey, and that SMS or app notifications aren't accepted.
questions.stem: What should you configure?
options: On activation, require Azure MFA
An authentication context whose Conditional Access policy requires phishing-resistant strength
Require ticket information on activation
Require multifactor authentication on active assignment
questions.explain: Authentication context links PIM activation to a Conditional Access policy, which can require an authentication strength. The plain MFA setting accepts any MFA method, ticket information is free text, and MFA on active assignment applies when an admin creates the assignment.

questions.stem: Which settings are on the Activation tab of a Microsoft Entra role's PIM settings? Select THREE.
options: Allow permanent eligible assignment
Require justification on activation
Require ticket information on activation
Send notifications when members are assigned as eligible
Require approval to activate
questions.explain: Activation covers maximum duration, MFA or authentication context, justification, ticket information and approval. Permanent eligible assignment is on the Assignment tab, and assignment notifications are on the Notification tab.

questions.stem: A Global Administrator without any Azure RBAC role must make Contributor on a subscription eligible-only in PIM. Put the steps in order.
options: Elevate access to get User Access Administrator at root scope
In PIM, open Azure resources and select the subscription
Edit the Contributor role settings for that subscription
Add an eligible assignment of Contributor
questions.explain: A Global Administrator without Azure access first elevates access. PIM then needs the subscription selected, settings configured per role and scope, and an eligible assignment added.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: PIM role settings set on a subscription are inherited by the resource groups in it.
An activated eligible Contributor assignment at subscription scope grants Contributor on that subscription's resource groups.
For Azure resource roles, Global Administrators are the default approvers when approval is required but none are selected.

questions.explain: Role settings apply per role and scope and aren't inherited. Role assignments follow Azure RBAC inheritance. Azure resource roles have no default approvers, so you must select at least one.

questions.stem: Which Azure role on a subscription lets you manage PIM role settings for that subscription?
options: Contributor
Reader
Owner
Security Reader
questions.explain: Managing PIM settings and assignments for Azure resources needs Owner or User Access Administrator, because both can write role assignments. Contributor, Reader and Security Reader can't.

questions.stem: Which groups can you manage with PIM for Groups? Select TWO.
options: Group with dynamic membership rules
Cloud security group that isn't role-assignable
Group synchronized from on-premises AD DS
Microsoft 365 group
questions.explain: PIM for Groups supports Microsoft Entra security groups and Microsoft 365 groups, role-assignable or not. Dynamic membership groups and groups synchronized from on-premises aren't supported.

questions.stem: You want admins to get the Exchange Administrator role just-in-time by activating membership of a group with PIM for Groups. Which TWO are required?
options: The group must be created as role-assignable
Every eligible member needs a Microsoft Entra ID P2 or ID Governance licence
The group must use dynamic membership
The group must be synchronized from on-premises
Eligible members must already be Global Administrators
questions.explain: Only role-assignable groups can hold Entra role assignments, and every eligible member or owner needs P2 or ID Governance. Dynamic and synced groups aren't supported, and members don't need other roles.

questions.stem: Group owners must get approval before they activate ownership in PIM for Groups, while members activate membership without approval. How do you configure this?
options: Create two groups, one for owners and one for members
Set an access review with different reviewers for owners
Use a Conditional Access policy that targets group owners
Set the Owner and Member role settings separately for the group in PIM
questions.explain: PIM for Groups has separate role settings for Member and Owner, each with its own approval, MFA, justification and duration. You don't need extra groups, reviews or Conditional Access.

questions.stem: An approver doesn't act on a pending PIM activation request. After how long must the requester submit a new request?
options: 24 hours
1 hour
8 hours
7 days
questions.explain: Approvers have 24 hours to approve a PIM request. After that the request can't be approved and the eligible user must submit a new one. The window can't be configured.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: An approver can approve their own PIM activation request.
When several approvers are configured, the first approver to approve or deny resolves the request.
A user can deactivate a role before the activation duration ends.

questions.explain: Approvers can't approve their own requests. The first approver's decision resolves the request and the others are notified. Users can deactivate early when they finish.

questions.stem: A role requires approval to activate. Put the steps of a successful activation in order.
options: The user selects Activate on the eligible role in My roles
The user enters duration and justification and completes MFA
An approver approves the request on Approve requests
The role becomes active for the chosen duration
The role deactivates when the duration ends
questions.explain: Activation starts from My roles, gathers the required details and MFA, waits for approval, then grants the role for the chosen time before it deactivates automatically.

questions.stem: Which PIM alert for Microsoft Entra roles has High severity?
options: Too many Global Administrators
Roles are assigned outside PIM
Roles don't require MFA for activation
Administrators aren't using their privileged roles
questions.explain: Roles are assigned outside PIM is the High-severity alert, because standing assignments made outside PIM bypass its controls. Too many Global Administrators, roles not requiring MFA, and unused privileged roles are Low severity.

questions.stem: Auditors need PIM activation history for the past 12 months. Resource audit shows only recent data. What should you do?
options: Increase the Resource audit retention in PIM settings
Ask each administrator to export My audit
Configure diagnostic settings to send audit logs to a Log Analytics workspace or storage account
Enable the Potential stale accounts alert
questions.explain: PIM audit history in the portal covers 30 days. To keep it longer, route Entra audit logs with diagnostic settings. PIM has no retention setting, My audit shows only the user's own activity, and alerts don't store history.

questions.stem: You query PIM role activations that were sent to Log Analytics. Complete the query.
questions.code:
____
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where OperationName has "Add member to role"
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, InitiatedBy, TargetResources
options: SigninLogs
AADProvisioningLogs
AADRiskyUsers
AuditLogs
questions.explain: PIM activations and assignments are audit events, so they're in the AuditLogs table with InitiatedBy and TargetResources columns. Sign-in, provisioning and risky-user tables don't record role membership changes.

questions.stem: Which configuration matches Microsoft guidance for an emergency access account?
options: Cloud-only account on the *.onmicrosoft.com domain with a permanent active Global Administrator assignment
Account synchronized from AD DS with an eligible Global Administrator assignment
Federated account whose MFA uses one administrator's mobile phone
Cloud-only account with Global Administrator eligible and approval required
questions.explain: Break-glass accounts should be cloud-only on onmicrosoft.com, so they don't depend on federation or sync, and hold permanent active Global Administrator. Eligible or approval-gated assignments, and dependence on one person's phone, can fail in an emergency.

questions.stem: Which TWO actions follow Microsoft's recommendations for emergency access accounts?
options: Tie each account's MFA to one administrator's personal phone
Register a FIDO2 passkey as a phishing-resistant method
Make the Global Administrator assignment eligible with approval
Exclude the accounts from blocking Conditional Access policies by using a dedicated group
questions.explain: Use a phishing-resistant method such as a FIDO2 passkey, and exclude the accounts from Conditional Access policies that block or restrict sign-in. Don't depend on one person's device, and keep the role permanently active.

questions.stem: You create an Azure Monitor alert that fires whenever an emergency access account signs in. Complete the query.
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where ____ == "00aa00aa-bb11-cc22-dd33-44ee44ee44ee"
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, ResultType
options: AppId
UserId
CorrelationId
ResourceId
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends filtering SigninLogs on the accounts' object IDs, stored in UserId, with a threshold above 0. AppId identifies the application, CorrelationId links related events, and ResourceId is the target resource.

questions.stem: Your tenant used Microsoft Entra ID Free and upgraded to P1 today. Can you see audit log entries from 20 days ago in the admin center?
options: Yes; P1 retention of 30 days applies backwards
Yes; audit logs are always kept for 90 days
No; only data still inside the 7-day Free retention is available
No; audit logs need P2
questions.explain: Retention changes aren't retroactive. Free keeps audit and sign-in logs for 7 days, so older data is gone unless it was exported. From now on, P1 keeps 30 days.

questions.stem: Outlook silently refreshes a user's token in the background. In which sign-in log is this recorded?
options: Interactive user sign-ins
Service principal sign-ins
Managed identity sign-ins
Non-interactive user sign-ins
questions.explain: Token-based sign-ins that a client does for a user, without the user entering a credential, are non-interactive user sign-ins. Service principal and managed identity logs cover app identities, not users.

questions.stem: Which sign-in log types record authentication by non-human identities? Select TWO.
options: Interactive user sign-ins
Service principal sign-ins
Non-interactive user sign-ins
Managed identity sign-ins
questions.explain: Service principal sign-ins are apps using secrets or certificates, and managed identity sign-ins are Azure-managed identities. Interactive and non-interactive sign-ins both belong to users.

questions.stem: A user can't reach an app and you think a Conditional Access policy blocked them. Where do you find which policy caused the failure?
options: On the Conditional Access tab of the user's sign-in log entry
In the audit logs, under the Policy category
In the provisioning logs for the app
In Identity Secure Score improvement actions
questions.explain: Each sign-in log entry has a Conditional Access tab listing the policies evaluated and their result. Audit logs record policy changes, not evaluations, provisioning logs cover account sync, and Secure Score gives recommendations.

questions.stem: In the provisioning logs for a SaaS app, a user's event has the status Skipped. What is the most likely cause?
options: The user's password expired
The user is out of scope, for example not assigned to the app
A Conditional Access policy blocked the user's sign-in
The user failed MFA
questions.explain: Skipped usually means the provisioning service didn't process the object, often because it's out of scope through assignment or a scoping filter. Password, Conditional Access and MFA issues affect sign-in, not provisioning.

questions.stem: You need to stream Microsoft Entra sign-in logs to Log Analytics. Put the steps in order.
options: Create a Log Analytics workspace in an Azure subscription
In the Entra admin center, open Diagnostic settings and add a setting
Select the SignInLogs category
Choose Send to Log Analytics workspace and pick the workspace
Save, then query the data once it arrives
questions.explain: The destination must exist first. Then you add a diagnostic setting, choose the categories and destination, and save. Data arrives after a delay.

questions.stem: Your SOC uses Splunk. You need to stream Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs to it in near real time. Which diagnostic setting destination should you use?
options: Archive to a storage account
Send to Log Analytics workspace
Stream to an event hub
Send to a Microsoft Sentinel watchlist
questions.explain: Event Hubs is the destination for streaming to non-Microsoft SIEMs such as Splunk. Storage accounts archive, Log Analytics is for Azure Monitor querying, and a watchlist isn't a diagnostic destination.

questions.stem: Compliance needs Microsoft Entra audit logs kept for three years at the lowest cost. They'll rarely be read. Which destination should you choose?
options: Log Analytics workspace
Event hub
The Entra admin center's built-in retention
Storage account
questions.explain: A storage account is the cheap long-term archive for rarely read logs. Log Analytics is for querying and costs more to keep data, an event hub streams but doesn't store long term, and built-in retention is 30 days at most.

questions.stem: Which log categories can you select in Microsoft Entra diagnostic settings? Select THREE.
options: NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
DeviceComplianceOrg
AuditLogs
SecurityAlert
ProvisioningLogs
questions.explain: Entra diagnostic settings offer categories such as AuditLogs, SignInLogs, NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs and ProvisioningLogs. DeviceComplianceOrg is an Intune log category, and SecurityAlert is a Microsoft Sentinel table.

questions.stem: Complete the query to list the 10 users with the most failed sign-ins in the last 7 days.
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType != "0"
| ____ FailedCount = count() by UserPrincipalName
| top 10 by FailedCount
options: summarize
project
extend
distinct
questions.explain: summarize groups rows and calculates aggregates such as count() by a column. project and extend shape columns without aggregating, and distinct returns unique values but can't use count().

questions.stem: Complete the query to chart interactive sign-ins per hour over the last day.
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize count() by ____(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| render timechart
options: ago
bin
format_datetime
todatetime
questions.explain: bin() rounds timestamps into fixed buckets, here one hour, for time charts. ago() gives a time relative to now, format_datetime returns a string, and todatetime converts values, so none of them bucket by an interval.

questions.stem: You need to count token-based sign-ins that client apps made for users, by app, over the last day. Complete the query.
questions.code:
____
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize count() by AppDisplayName
options: SigninLogs
AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs
questions.explain: Token-based sign-ins on a user's behalf go to AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs. SigninLogs holds interactive sign-ins only, and the service principal and managed identity tables cover non-human identities.

questions.stem: Before blocking legacy authentication, you need to find which users and apps still use it. Which Microsoft Entra workbook should you use?
options: Sensitive Operations Report
Cross-tenant access activity
Authentication prompts analysis
Sign-ins using legacy authentication
questions.explain: The legacy authentication workbook shows sign-ins that use legacy protocols. The Sensitive Operations Report tracks risky configuration changes, cross-tenant access activity tracks B2B traffic, and authentication prompts analysis looks at MFA prompts.

questions.stem: Microsoft Entra workbooks show no data for your tenant. Which TWO are required for them to work?
options: A Log Analytics workspace
A diagnostic setting that sends Entra logs to the workspace
An Event Hubs namespace
A storage account in the same region as the tenant
questions.explain: Workbooks query Log Analytics, so you need a workspace and a diagnostic setting sending Entra logs to it. Event hubs and storage accounts are other destinations that workbooks don't query.

questions.stem: How often is the Identity Secure Score recalculated?
options: Every 24 hours
Every hour
Every 7 days
Only when an admin selects Refresh
questions.explain: Microsoft evaluates your configuration and recalculates the Identity Secure Score every 24 hours, so changes can take up to a day to show.

questions.stem: Contoso enforces MFA with a non-Microsoft identity provider for an improvement action Entra can't verify. Which status gives the points?
options: Risk accepted
Resolved through third party
Planned
To address
questions.explain: Resolved through third party (or alternate mitigation) awards the points even though Microsoft can't verify it. Risk accepted gives no points, and Planned and To address mark work not yet done.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Marking an improvement action as Risk accepted earns its full points.
Identity Secure Score is the identity category of Microsoft Secure Score.
Partly completing an action, such as MFA for half of the users in scope, can earn partial points.

questions.explain: Risk accepted hides the action but earns no points. Identity Secure Score is the identity part of Microsoft Secure Score. Many actions score in proportion to how many users are covered.
